State precedence

  • Hover and Focused: Focused wins. The ring stays drawn while the pointer is over the circle; hover only steps the fill.
  • Hover and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled circle keeps its resting look under the pointer and takes no click.
  • Selected and Hover: both show. The .14 selected fill stays under the pointer; hover adds the pointer cursor and nothing to the fill.
  • Selected and Expanded: Not applicable: a key is a toggle or a fold key, never both; the caller passes one of the two props.
  • Expanded and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled fold key keeps aria-expanded and takes no click.
  • Selected and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled toggle drops to the disabled ink and takes no click.
  • Pressed and Focused: both show. The ring stays drawn while the circle is held down.
  • Hinted and Pressed: Pressed wins. The press puts the hint away.
  • Hinted and Hover: both show. The hint follows the hover after its delay.
  • Hinted and Focused: both show. The hint arrives with the ring, with no delay.
  • Hinted and Selected: both show. The hint names a toggle whatever its state.
  • Hinted and Expanded: both show on a fold key, until the click that folds puts the hint away; on a key with popup, Expanded wins, and the hint stays away while the key's own menu or dialog is open.
  • Hinted and Disabled: both show. A disabled key still says what it is, and why it is blocked when it has a description.
  • Focused and Disabled: both show. A disabled key takes focus and the ring, so a keyboard user can reach its hint; Enter and Space do nothing.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
The pointer enters or leavesinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)background-color, colorThe fill and the ink change at once: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] * rule removes the transition.
The pointer is held downinputpress (--dur-press + --ease-standard)transformThe circle stays at rest: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] * rule removes the transition.
The pointer presses downinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)background-colorThe fill changes at once, by the same rule.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
iconstringThe id from ../icons.ts; the glyph is drawn in code.
titlestringThe accessible name (aria-label) and the hint's text.
controls?stringThe id of the region a fold key shows and hides: sets aria-controls.
description?stringA second line under the name in the hint, and the key's accessible description: why it is disabled ("Type a message first"), what it will do.
disabled?booleanBlocks the click and drops the glyph to the disabled ink.
expanded?booleanA fold key: sets aria-expanded to whether the region it folds is showing now.
onClick?((event: MouseEvent) => void)Runs on click.
popup?IconButtonPopupThe key opens a popup of this kind: sets aria-haspopup.
selected?booleanA toggle-style icon button: sets aria-pressed and the .14 selected fill.
shortcut?stringThe shortcut that runs the same action, as the user reads it ("Ctrl+Z", "F9"): a key cap in the hint and aria-keyshortcuts on the button.
size?IconButtonSizeThe box size.
variant?IconButtonVariantThe look.
  • icon: the id from src/icons.ts; the glyph is drawn in code, never an image.
  • title: the accessible name (aria-label) and the text of the layer's hint; an icon alone has no name without it. No native title attribute is rendered.
  • variant: the look; defaults to ghost.
  • size: the circle; md is 24px with a 14px glyph, sm is 20px with a 12px glyph.
  • selected: sets aria-pressed and the .14 selected fill.
  • expanded: a fold key; sets aria-expanded to whether the region it folds is showing.
  • controls: the id of the region a fold key shows and hides, or of the popup a key opens; sets aria-controls.
  • popup: the key opens a popup of this kind; sets aria-haspopup. menu for a list of actions, listbox for a list of values to pick one from, dialog for a popover holding fields or other controls.
  • shortcut: the shortcut that runs the same action, as the user reads it (Ctrl+Z, F9): a key cap after the name in the hint, and aria-keyshortcuts on the button. A title that ends in the shortcut in brackets ("Undo (Ctrl+Z)") still draws the cap; its name keeps the bracket, so no aria-keyshortcuts repeats it.
  • description: a second line under the name in the hint, tied to the button as its accessible description (aria-describedby): why the key is disabled, what it will do. Never the name.
  • disabled: blocks the click and drops the glyph to the disabled ink. It sets aria-disabled="true", never the native disabled, so the key stays in the Tab order and under the pointer and its hint still shows.
  • onClick: runs on click; a disabled circle never fires it.

Usage

When to use

  • The action is one glyph a tooltip can name: close, attach, send, stop, add.
  • The control sits in a tool bar, a panel header or a toolbar row where a label would crowd the row.

When not to use

  • The action needs a label to be understood. Use Button instead.
  • The control is a list item with a name. Use Row instead.
  • The glyph is a status rather than an action. Use Chip instead.

Rules

  • rule/icon-button-name: When an icon button is rendered, pass title for every use, because the glyph alone leaves the accessible name empty and a screen reader announces "button". Evidence: app 3/3 composer icon buttons, src/components/AssistantPane.tsx. Check: test src/ui/IconButton.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <IconButton icon="close" /> — no name.
  • Do: <IconButton icon="close" title="Close the panel" />
  • rule/icon-button-one-inverted: When a toolbar row holds icon buttons, keep at most 1 inverted circle, because the ink-coloured circle is the row's primary action and a second one splits the eye. Evidence: measured 1 inverted send button in the composer toolbar, docs/system/decisions.md. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: two variant="inverted" circles in the composer row.
  • Do: 1 inverted send and ghost for attach and stop.
  • rule/icon-button-fold-expanded: When an icon button folds and unfolds a region, pass expanded with the region's state and controls with the region's id, and leave selected unset, because a title that flips between Show and Hide is the only signal otherwise, and a screen reader hears 2 unrelated buttons where there is 1 key that is collapsed or expanded. Evidence: app 3/3 fold keys (the layers, the properties, the changes row), src/components/LayersPanel.tsx. Check: test src/ui/IconButton.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <IconButton icon="chevron-down" size="sm" title={open() ? "Hide the layers" : "Show the layers"} selected={open()} />
  • Do: <IconButton icon="chevron-down" size="sm" title={open() ? "Hide the layers" : "Show the layers"} expanded={open()} controls="layers-body" />
  • rule/icon-button-popup-kind: When an icon button opens something that floats over the page, pass popup with its kind (1 of menu, listbox, dialog, matching the role of what opens), expanded with whether it is open, and controls with its id while it is rendered, and leave selected unset, because a key with no aria-haspopup is announced as a plain button and the menu it opens arrives unannounced. Evidence: single use src/components/MenuBar.tsx:194, the narrow window's Main menu key, which sets the attribute from outside on mount. Check: test src/ui/IconButton.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <IconButton icon="list" title="Main menu" expanded={open()} /> with setAttribute("aria-haspopup", "menu") on mount.
  • Do: <IconButton icon="list" title="Main menu" popup="menu" expanded={open()} controls={open() ? "main-menu" : undefined} />
  • rule/icon-button-no-native-title: When an icon button is styled or wrapped, add 0 hints of its own (no title attribute set from outside, no Tooltip around it), because the component already shows its title in the layer's hint box and a second hint stacks on the first. Evidence: app 31/31 icon buttons in the running shell render no title attribute, measured in the browser 2026-11-11. Check: test src/ui/IconButton.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tooltip text="Close"><IconButton icon="close" title="Close" /></Tooltip>
  • Do: <IconButton icon="close" title="Close the panel" />
  • rule/icon-button-shortcut-prop: When an icon button's action has a shortcut, pass it as shortcut and keep it out of title, because the hint draws it as 1 key cap and the button says it through aria-keyshortcuts, while a bracket in the title puts "(Ctrl+Z)" into the accessible name a speech-input user has to say; the parsed bracket form stays for a caller that has not moved, and no call site in the app uses it now (the tool strip's five, the title bar's three and the composer's send and stop pass shortcut). Evidence: app 9/31 icon buttons in the running shell carry a shortcut in brackets in their name, measured in the browser 2026-11-11. Check: test src/ui/IconButton.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <IconButton icon="undo" title="Undo (Ctrl+Z)" />
  • Do: <IconButton icon="undo" title="Undo" shortcut="Ctrl+Z" />
  • rule/icon-button-disabled-reason: When an icon button is disabled by something the user can fix, pass the reason as description in 1 short sentence, because the disabled key stays focusable and hoverable for exactly this, and its name alone says what it is and 0 words about why it is dead. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:939, the composer's send key, disabled while the message is empty with no reason given. Check: test src/ui/IconButton.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <IconButton icon="send" title="Send" disabled={empty()} />
  • Do: <IconButton icon="send" title="Send" disabled={empty()} description={empty() ? "Type a message first" : undefined} />

Content

  • rule/icon-button-title-sentence: When title is written, name the action in sentence case with no full stop (Close the panel, Send, Stop), because the same string is the hint and the accessible name. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:857, the "Attach a picture (or paste, or drop one)" label. Check: review src/components/AssistantPane.tsx.
  • Don't: title="close panel."
  • Do: title="Close the panel"

Anti-slop

  • rule/icon-button-canonical-element: When a surface needs an icon action, render IconButton rather than a raw <button> with a hand-sized glyph, because the replaced classes hard-code 3 different box sizes and their own hover opacities. Evidence: app 10/10 lines across src/assistant.css and src/components/AssistantPane.tsx, rg -c "assistant-icon|assistant-attachment-x" src. Check: review src/ui/IconButton.tsx.
  • Don't: <button class="assistant-icon" onClick={stop}>…</button>
  • Do: <IconButton icon="stop" title="Stop" onClick={stop} />

Limits

  • rule/icon-button-row-limit: When a toolbar row holds more than 5 icon buttons, move the rest into a menu, because the measured composer row holds 3 at 24px each with 4px gaps and the row starts crowding the input past 5. Evidence: measured 3 actions at 24px with 4px gaps, docs/system/decisions.md. Check: review src/components/AssistantPane.tsx.
  • Don't: 6 circles in the composer's toolbar row.
  • Do: 3 circles in the row and the rest inside a menu.
  • rule/icon-button-touch-target: When 2 sm icon buttons sit side by side, keep at least 4px between them, because under a coarse pointer each 20px circle keeps its drawn size and takes a 24px target from an invisible ::after 2px past every edge, and closer circles overlap their targets. Evidence: measured 20px circle with a 24px ::after target, src/ui/ui.css:1137. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: .my-row .ui-icon-button--sm + .ui-icon-button--sm { margin-left: 0 } — two 24px targets on a 20px pitch.
  • Do: .my-row { display: flex; gap: var(--gap-4) }

Accessibility

Rests on the native <button> element, with the drawn glyph hidden from assistive tech. Disabled is the layer's own, shared with Button: aria-disabled="true" with the click refused on the button itself, because the native disabled takes a key out of the Tab order and, in some of the system webviews the desktop app runs in, out of the pointer's reach, and a key nobody can reach cannot say what it is or why it is blocked (docs/system/decisions.md, "Disabled controls").

Related

  • Button: when the action needs a visible label.
  • Chip: when the glyph and the text are a fact rather than an action.
  • Row: when the clickable band is a list item.
  • Tab: when the control brings one view of a strip to the front rather than toggling a setting; a closable tab draws its own close key.
  • Tooltip: the hint box this component shows by itself; wrap another control in it, never this one.
  • Kbd: the key cap the hint draws for a shortcut.
  • Checkbox: when the on/off belongs to a form's value rather than to a tool.
  • Toggle: when a setting is switched in place under a fixed name, its state drawn by the glyph and never by a fill: a list row's state keys, a bar's drafting settings.

Kbd

Description

It shows the key or shortcut that runs the action beside it, as a fact to read and never as a control.

import { Kbd } from "../../../../src/ui/Kbd";, source src/ui/Kbd.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/button-div (n/a: a cap takes no handler), trap/role-button (n/a: a cap has no role beyond the native <kbd>), trap/control-height (n/a: a cap is text on a hairline, not a control; its 18px box comes from the 16px line and the two hairlines).

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — a native <kbd> on one recipe. It replaces two hand-built caps, and the recipe kept is the command palette's (.palette-key): the UI face, the quiet ink --text-faint, the chip type size and a 16px line. The assistant's (.assistant-key: the mono face at the disabled ink --text-disabled, no line height) lost, because the disabled ink marks a control that cannot be used and a shortcut can, and because the palette's shortcuts are combinations ("Ctrl+Shift+S") that read as words in the UI face.

Examples

<Kbd>esc</Kbd> — the key that stops a running request, beside Stop.

Real uses, 5 call sites (rg -c "<Kbd" src/components → src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:4, src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:4):

  • src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:872 — the esc cap beside the Stop button on the run row over the composer, shown while a request runs.
  • src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:261 — each command's shortcut at the end of its palette row, written by shortcutLabel for the platform; a command with no shortcut draws no cap.
  • src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:282 — the palette footer's three caps (Enter, Tab, Esc) beside Run, Complete and Close.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
children?ElementThe key or shortcut as the user reads it: esc, Ctrl+Shift+P.
  • children: the key or shortcut as the user reads it: esc, Ctrl+Shift+P.

Usage

When to use

  • An action on screen has a key or a shortcut, and the user is helped by seeing it beside the action: Stop and esc, a palette command and its shortcut.

When not to use

  • The key should itself be clickable. Use Button instead, and put the cap beside it.
  • The text is a value or a keyword rather than a key (26 objects, a command's option). Use Chip instead.
  • The shortcut is a hint that should show only on hover. Use Tooltip instead.

Rules

  • rule/kbd-beside-action: When a cap is rendered, place it directly after the 1 action its key runs (the button, or the row's label), because a cap on its own names a key without saying what the key does. Evidence: app 2/2 caps follow their action, src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:691 and src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:140. Check: review src/components/AssistantPane.tsx.
  • Don't: <Kbd>esc</Kbd> alone on a status row.
  • Do: <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" onClick={stop}>Stop</Button><Kbd>esc</Kbd>
  • rule/kbd-not-a-control: When the shortcut's action must be clickable, put the handler on the Button or Row beside the cap rather than on the cap, because a <kbd> has no role and no tab stop, so a click handler on it is unreachable by keyboard. Evidence: app 2/2 caps take no handler, src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:844 and src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:144. Check: test src/ui/Kbd.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <span onClick={stop}><Kbd>esc</Kbd></span>
  • Do: <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" onClick={stop}>Stop</Button><Kbd>esc</Kbd>

Content

  • rule/kbd-shortcut-label: When a cap shows a combination of 2 or more keys, write it with shortcutLabel(shortcut, mac), because the platform decides between "Ctrl+Shift+Z" and the macOS symbols and a literal string is wrong on one of them. Evidence: single use src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:144. Check: review src/components/CommandPalette.tsx.
  • Don't: <Kbd>Ctrl+S</Kbd>
  • Do: <Kbd>{shortcutLabel("Cmd+S", mac)}</Kbd>

Anti-slop

  • rule/kbd-canonical-element: When a surface shows a key, render Kbd rather than a raw <kbd> with its own class, because the 2 replaced classes drew the same cap in 2 faces and 2 inks. Evidence: app 2/2 hand-built caps replaced (.assistant-key and .palette-key), src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:679 and src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:144. Check: review src/ui/Kbd.tsx.
  • Don't: <kbd class="assistant-key">esc</kbd>
  • Do: <Kbd>esc</Kbd>

Limits

Not applicable: a cap holds the one string shortcutLabel produces or one key name, and the widest rendered so far, the 12-character "Ctrl+Shift+S", measures 69.8px and fits its palette row; no length or count has been seen to break.

Row

Description

It is the full-width clickable band of a list: a menu item, a property row or a layer, marked current when it is the selected one.

import { Row } from "../../../../src/ui/Row";, source src/ui/Row.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/button-div, trap/role-button, trap/native-control, trap/list-dead-gap, trap/current-unmarked, trap/menu-navigation, trap/control-height, trap/focus-ring-shape, trap/hover-beats-focus, trap/disabled-still-hovers, trap/touch-hover-flash, trap/hover-unguarded.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — the 22px row, the 4px inset and the .14 selected fill are measured from the running Cursor 3.27.22 (docs/system/decisions.md and §5), and no registry item ships it.

Examples

<Row onClick={pick}>Layer 1</Row> — one layer in the layers list.

Real uses, 4 call sites (rg -c "<Row" src/components → src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:2, src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:1, src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:1):

  • src/components/AssistantPane.tsx — the setup sheet's provider rows and the composer's slash list (the commands a /word draft matches; selected marks the one the arrow keys are on); the chat tabs in the header moved onto Tab; the transcript's tool rows and the composer's toolbar row stay bespoke (the toolbar is a container, and the tool row carries a disclosure arrow and a note).
  • src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:126 — each command in the palette's list; selected marks the one the arrow keys are on, disabled the ones that cannot run now.
  • src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:53 — each layer's name band (is-current marks the current one); the toggle cluster beside it stays native buttons.
  • src/components/CommandPalette.tsx and the assistant's slash list in src/components/AssistantPane.tsx — their rows are <Row option> inside a role="listbox": out of the Tab order, lit by the list's one highlight.
  • (planned) src/components/MenuBar.tsx — .menu-row (1 use) moves onto <Row> once Row can carry the menuitem roles; the rows stay native buttons for now.
  • (planned) src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:202 — .prop-row (1 use) moves onto <Row> when the palette's rows become clickable; today they are display rows with an inline editor.
  • .layer-row (LayersPanel) stays bespoke because its row nests a toggle cluster, and a button cannot nest buttons.

State precedence

  • Hover and Selected: Selected wins. The .14 selected fill stays under the pointer; hover adds nothing to the fill.
  • Hover and Focused: Focused wins. The ring stays drawn while the pointer is over the row.
  • Hover and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled row keeps its resting look and takes no click.
  • Selected and Disabled: Disabled wins on a button. A disabled row is not the current one to the eye: it drops the .14 fill and shows the disabled ink, and aria-current="true" stays for assistive tech. On an option both show ("Option and Disabled" below).
  • Pressed and Focused: both show. The ring stays drawn while the row is held down.
  • Option and Hover: Option wins. An option takes no fill from the pointer; the listbox moves the one highlight to it by setting selected.
  • Option and Selected: both show. The active option takes the .14 fill and the full ink, as the current row does.
  • Option and Disabled: both show. A blocked option still takes the highlight when the keys reach it, at the disabled ink, and takes no click: in a listbox the fill is where the keys are, and a list with no fill has lost its cursor.
  • Clipped and Disabled: both show. The hint still reads the full label under the pointer.
  • Option and Focused: Not applicable: an option is never focused; the listbox's field keeps the focus and names the active option with aria-activedescendant.

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
The pointer enters or leavesinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)background-colorThe fill changes at once: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] rule removes the transition.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
children?ElementThe row's content: a label, and quiet trailing text such as a shortcut or a value.
disabled?booleanBlocks the click and drops the ink to the disabled step.
id?stringThe element's id, for the listbox's aria-activedescendant.
onClick?((event: MouseEvent) => void)Runs on click.
onPointerMove?((event: PointerEvent) => void)The pointer moved over the row: a listbox moves its highlight here.
option?booleanThe row is one option of a role="listbox" that owns the focus and the highlight: a role="option" band, no Tab stop and no hover fill of its own.
selected?booleanThe current row: the .14 fill, the full ink, and aria-current="true" (aria-selected on an option).
title?stringThe hint: what the row's text leaves out.
  • selected: the current row; sets aria-current="true" and the .14 fill. On an option it is the listbox's active option and sets aria-selected.
  • option: the row is one option of a role="listbox" that owns the focus and the highlight; it renders a role="option" band with no Tab stop and no hover fill.
  • id: the element's id, for the listbox's aria-activedescendant.
  • onPointerMove: the pointer moved over the row; a listbox moves its highlight here.
  • disabled: blocks the click and drops the ink to the disabled step.
  • title: the hint: what the row's text leaves out. It shows in the layer's hint box (after 0.4s under a mouse or a pen, at once when a key moves focus in) and is the row's accessible description (aria-describedby), never its name, and no native title attribute is rendered. A title that repeats the row's text adds nothing and is dropped. A clipped label needs no title: it shows in full by itself, with the title under it.
  • onClick: runs on click; a disabled row never fires it.
  • children: the row's content: a label, and quiet trailing text such as a shortcut.

Usage

When to use

  • One item of a list is clickable and runs one action: a menu item, a layer, a property.
  • The current item of that list must be marked for a screen reader as well as the eye.

When not to use

  • The action is a single control with a label. Use Button instead.
  • The row nests its own controls (a toggle cluster, a stepper). Use Button and IconButton in a bespoke band instead, because a button cannot nest buttons.
  • The band is a heading above a list rather than a row in it. Use SectionLabel instead.

Rules

  • rule/row-one-action: When a row runs an action, wire it on Row itself rather than on a label inside it, because a label-only hit area leaves dead space that reads as broken. Evidence: app 8/8 lines across src/chrome.css, src/components/MenuBar.tsx and src/styles.css, rg -c "menu-row" src. Check: test src/ui/Row.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Row><span onClick={pick}>Layer 1</span></Row>
  • Do: <Row onClick={pick}>Layer 1</Row>
  • rule/row-option-in-listbox: When rows are the items of a role="listbox" whose field keeps the focus, pass option on each with an id, mark the active one with selected and move it from onPointerMove, because a <button> inside a role="option" adds 1 Tab stop per row and its own hover fill, so two rows are lit at once: the pointer's and the keyboard's. Evidence: single use src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:244, a Row button inside a .palette-option wrapper. Check: test src/ui/Row.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <div role="option" aria-selected={lit}><Row selected={lit} onClick={run}>Line</Row></div>
  • Do: <Row option id="command-0" selected={lit} onPointerMove={light} onClick={run}>Line</Row>
  • rule/row-current-marked: When a list has a current item, pass selected on it, because the .14 fill alone is colour and a screen reader needs aria-current="true" to hear it. Evidence: app 3/3 list surfaces draw a current row, src/styles.css. Check: test src/ui/Row.test.tsx.
  • Don't: a hand-painted background on the current row with no aria-current.
  • Do: <Row selected>Current layer</Row>

Content

  • rule/row-trailing-quiet: When a row carries a shortcut or a value, put it after the label in the dim ink (--text-faint), because the label is what the user scans and the trailing text is secondary. Evidence: single use src/components/MenuBar.tsx:231, the shortcut span. Check: review src/components/MenuBar.tsx.
  • Don't: a shortcut before the label.
  • Do: <Row>Save<span class="row-shortcut">Ctrl+S</span></Row>

Anti-slop

  • rule/row-canonical-element: When a surface needs a list band, render Row rather than a div with an onClick, because a div has no role, no focus and no disabled state, and the replaced classes repeat hover and selected by hand. Evidence: app 23/23 lines across 7 files, rg -c "prop-row|menu-row|assistant-row|assistant-tool" src. Check: review src/ui/Row.tsx.
  • Don't: <div class="menu-row" onClick={pick}>Open</div>
  • Do: <Row onClick={pick}>Open</Row>

Limits

  • rule/row-label-limit: When a row's label runs past 40 characters at the 260px sidebar, clip it with an ellipsis on the label's own element and leave title for what the hint adds, because the measured row is 22px tall and the sidebar 260px wide, and the hint already reads a clipped label in full on its first line. Evidence: measured 22px row and 260px sidebar, docs/system/decisions.md. Check: review src/styles.css.
  • Don't: a 60-character layer name that overflows the row.
  • Do: <Row><span class="row-label">{name}</span></Row> with overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis on the label, and no title that repeats it.
  • rule/row-touch-target: When rows stack in a list, let the list's height follow its rows rather than fixing it to a multiple of 22px, because under a coarse pointer each row grows from 22px to the 24px control height (rows stack with 0 gap, so an overhanging target would only overlap the next row) and a fixed list would cut its last rows. Evidence: measured 22px row, 24px under a coarse pointer, src/ui/ui.css:1165. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: .my-list { height: calc(var(--control-h-row) * 8); overflow: hidden }
  • Do: .my-list { max-height: calc(var(--control-h-input) * 8); overflow-y: auto }

Related

  • Button: when the control is an action rather than a list item.
  • SectionLabel: when the band is the heading above a list rather than a row in it.
  • IconButton: when the row's trailing control is a glyph action.
  • Tooltip: the hint box a row's title and its clipped label show in. A Tooltip wrapped around a row with no title still speaks; give the row its title instead of wrapping it.
  • Tab: when the control brings one view of a strip to the front rather than being one band of a list.
  • Kbd: when the text is the key that runs an action, shown at the end of the row.
  • Select: when the list is a short set of values behind one closed control rather than rows on the page.

SectionLabel

Description

It names a panel's section as a real heading, so a screen reader can jump between the sections by heading.

import { SectionLabel } from "../../../../src/ui/SectionLabel";, source src/ui/SectionLabel.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/native-control.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — the 11px uppercase header is measured from the running Cursor 3.27.22 (docs/system/decisions.md), and no registry item ships it.

Examples

<SectionLabel>Layers</SectionLabel> — the heading above the layers list.

Real uses, 4 call sites (rg -c "<SectionLabel" src/components → src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:5, src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:1, src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:1):

  • src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:759 and :542 — the setup sheet's "Provider" and "Connection" headings.
  • src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:83 — the "Layers" heading.
  • src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:64 — the "Properties" heading.

import { SectionLabel } from "../../../../src/ui/SectionLabel";

export default function InLayersPanel() {

    <div class="layers-head">
      <SectionLabel>Layers</SectionLabel>
    </div>
  );
}

Variants

Not applicable

Not applicable: no variant axes — a section label is one heading; its size, weight and ink come from the one recipe, and anything that looks different is a different role (a pane title, a tab).

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
RestThe heading is rendered.Read it; jump to it by heading navigation.The bold uppercase label at the faint ink, with no added letter spacing (the measured header).test
Long labelThe section's name is wider than its panel.Read it; the label does not wrap.The label runs to the panel's edge; a longer name is the caller's problem to shorten.by hand

State precedence

  • Rest and Long label: Not applicable: the heading has no other state; a long label is the same resting state with more text.

Motion

Not applicable: no motion — the heading never changes state, and its ink comes from the tokens.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
children?ElementThe section's name.
  • children: the section's name: one or two words, the same noun the panel uses elsewhere.

Usage

When to use

  • A panel or a popover holds more than one group, and each group needs a name a screen reader can jump to.
  • The name sits above a list, a table or a group of controls as their heading.

When not to use

  • The text is an action rather than a name. Use Button instead.
  • The text is a value or a status. Use Chip instead.
  • The text is a list item the user can pick. Use Row instead.

Rules

  • rule/section-label-heading-element: When a section label is rendered, keep it an <h2>, because the element is what lets a screen reader jump between panels and a styled <div> reads as plain text. Evidence: app 3/3 panels draw a section header, src/components/LayersPanel.tsx. Check: test src/ui/SectionLabel.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <div class="section-label">Layers</div>
  • Do: <SectionLabel>Layers</SectionLabel>
  • rule/section-label-not-action: When a heading needs a control beside it, put the control outside SectionLabel rather than inside it, because a button inside a heading joins the heading's name and garbles heading navigation. Evidence: app 2/2 panel heads keep their controls in the bar, src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx. Check: review src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: <SectionLabel>Layers <IconButton icon="plus" title="New layer" /></SectionLabel>
  • Do: <div class="head"><SectionLabel>Layers</SectionLabel><IconButton icon="plus" title="New layer" /></div>

Content

  • rule/section-label-one-noun: When the label's text is written, use 1 noun in title case (Layers, Properties, Selection), because the label is uppercased by CSS and a sentence reads as shouting. Evidence: single use src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:79, the label "Layers". Check: review src/components/LayersPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: <SectionLabel>Here are your layers</SectionLabel>
  • Do: <SectionLabel>Layers</SectionLabel>

Anti-slop

  • rule/section-label-canonical-element: When a surface needs a section header, render SectionLabel rather than a styled <div> or a bespoke class, because the replaced class is a bare rule with no role and drifts per panel. Evidence: app 3/3 lines across 2 panels and src/styles.css, rg -c "section-label" src/components src/styles.css. Check: review src/ui/SectionLabel.tsx.
  • Don't: <div class="section-label">Properties</div>
  • Do: <SectionLabel>Properties</SectionLabel>

Limits

  • rule/section-label-word-limit: When a section's name runs past 2 words, shorten it to 1 or 2 words, because the measured header row is 22px at 11px type and a third word starts clipping in a 260px sidebar. Evidence: measured 22px header at 11px type, docs/system/decisions.md. Check: review src/components/LayersPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: <SectionLabel>Layer visibility and lock state</SectionLabel>
  • Do: <SectionLabel>Layers</SectionLabel>

Accessibility

Rests on the native <h2> element: heading role and level come from the platform, and heading navigation works without ARIA.

Keyboard

KeyWhere focus isEffectFocus afterChecked by

ARIA

PartRoleAccessible name fromStates and propertiesAnnouncedChecked by
The headingheading level 2 (native <h2>)Its text contentNone: the level comes from the element"Layers, heading level 2"test

Tokens

PartStateToken
The textall--font-chip, --text-faint
The weightall700 (the one weight the system draws headings at)
The trackingallnone: the measured header is 11px bold capitals at the face's own spacing (docs/system/typography.md)

Related

  • Row: when the text is a clickable list item rather than a heading.
  • Chip: when the text is a compact value.
  • Button: when the text is an action.

Select

Description

It lets the user pick one value from a short, known list, and hands the pick back to the caller, who owns the value.

import { Select } from "../../../../src/ui/Select";, source src/ui/Select.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/native-control, trap/control-height, trap/field-label, trap/label-unbound, trap/field-error-link, trap/field-keeps-input, trap/select-value-lost, trap/select-empty-value, trap/select-async (n/a: the choices are a prop, never fetched by the component), trap/touch-input-zoom, trap/touch-hover-flash, trap/hover-unguarded, trap/focus-ring-shape, trap/hover-beats-focus, trap/disabled-still-hovers.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — a native <select> under a drawn face in Field's measured recipe (the 24px box, the hairline stroke, the focus edge; docs/system/decisions.md), and no registry item ships it.

Examples

<Select value={layer} options={layers} ariaLabel="Layer" onChange={setLayer} /> — the layer an object is on, picked from the drawing's layers.

Real uses, 1 call site (rg -c "<Select" src/components → src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:1):

  • src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:208 — the palette's choice rows (layer, linetype, colour): variant="inline" size="sm" align="end", mixed with the *VARIES* placeholder when the picked objects disagree.

Example: A layer picked from four, in the field recipe. (docs/system/examples/select/default.tsx)

import { Select } from "../../../../src/ui/Select";

const LAYERS = [
  { value: "0", label: "0" },
  { value: "walls", label: "Walls" },
  { value: "doors", label: "Doors" },
  { value: "furniture", label: "Furniture" },
];

export default function Default() {
  return <Select value="walls" options={LAYERS} ariaLabel="Layer" onChange={() => undefined} />;

Variants

variant

  • field: the form control, stroked and filled at rest, beside a Field. The default. Used at 0 call sites.
  • inline: a value in a dense list row; no stroke and no fill until the pointer or the keyboard is on it, with the arrow always drawn. Used at 0 call sites (the palette's 3 choice rows are planned).

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
RestThe control holds a value.Open the list, change the value by key, Tab away.The value's label and the chevron; a label wider than the box ends in an ellipsis before the arrow.test
HoverThe pointer is over the control, on a device with a hover pointer.Press to open the list.The pointer cursor; inline also takes the hairline stroke and the field fill.by hand
FocusedThe control takes focus by a press or Tab.Arrow keys and typed letters change the value; Space, Enter or Alt+ArrowDown open the list.The stroke takes the focus ink and the 1px ring draws at offset -1; inline takes the field fill.by hand
OpenThe user opens the list.Pick a choice, or Escape to leave the value as it was.The platform's own list (a popup on desktop, a picker on a phone).by hand
Off-list valuevalue is not among options.Keep it, or pick a listed choice; the off-list value stays the first choice until the caller's value changes.The value itself, shown and listed first.test
MixedThe caller passes mixed.Open the list and pick; the first pick replaces every differing value.The placeholder text (such as *VARIES*) in place of a value; it is not in the list.test
InvalidThe caller passes invalid.Pick another choice; the caller clears invalid when it accepts one.aria-invalid="true", and the caller's error line tied by describedBy; the stroke takes the error ink.test
DisabledThe caller passes disabled.Nothing: no list, no focus.The value and the chevron at the disabled ink; the cursor stays default.test
ClippedThe value's label is wider than the box.Rest the pointer on the control, or Tab to it, to read the whole label in the hint.The ellipsis; the hint's first line is the full label.test

Example: A refused choice at the error stroke, with the line that says why. (docs/system/examples/select/invalid.tsx)

import { Select } from "../../../../src/ui/Select";

const LAYERS = [
  { value: "0", label: "0" },
  { value: "walls", label: "Walls" },
  { value: "doors", label: "Doors" },
  { value: "furniture", label: "Furniture" },
];

export default function Invalid() {
  return (
    <div>
      <Select value="furniture" options={LAYERS} ariaLabel="Layer" invalid describedBy="layer-error" onChange={() => undefined} />
      <span id="layer-error">Furniture is locked. Pick a layer that takes new objects.</span>
    </div>
  );
}

State precedence

  • Focused and Hover: Focused wins. The focus stroke and the ring stay under the pointer.
  • Invalid and Focused: both show. The stroke keeps the error ink and the ring draws one line inside it.
  • Invalid and Hover: Invalid wins. The error stroke stays under the pointer.
  • Invalid and Mixed: both show. The placeholder stays in the quiet ink inside the error stroke.
  • Mixed and Off-list value: Mixed wins. The placeholder shows and value is not listed.
  • Mixed and Focused: both show. The placeholder stays until a choice is picked.
  • Mixed and Clipped: both show. A placeholder wider than the box clips and the hint reads it in full.
  • Disabled and Hover: Disabled wins. A disabled inline control takes no stroke and no fill under the pointer.
  • Disabled and Mixed: Disabled wins. The placeholder drops to the disabled ink.
  • Disabled and Invalid: Disabled wins on the ink, and the error stroke stays; the caller clears invalid before it locks a control nobody can correct.
  • Disabled and Clipped: both show. The hint still reads the full label under the pointer.
  • Open and Focused: both show. The control keeps its focus stroke while the platform's list is up.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
Focus arrives or leavesinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)border-color, background-colorThe stroke and the fill change at once: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] * rule removes the transition.
The pointer enters or leaves an inline controlinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)border-color, background-colorThe same: no transition plays.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
optionsreadonly SelectOption[]The choices, in the order the list shows them.
align?SelectAlignThe side the value sits on.
ariaLabel?stringThe accessible name when no visible <label> is tied to the control.
describedBy?stringThe id of the help line or the error line beside the control (several, space-separated): sets aria-describedby.
disabled?booleanBlocks the list and drops the ink to the disabled step.
invalid?booleanThe value is refused: sets aria-invalid and the error stroke.
mixed?booleanThe selection holds differing values: the placeholder shows in the quiet ink, and the first pick replaces them all.
onChange?((value: string) => void)Runs when the user picks a choice, with its value.
placeholder?stringWhat the control reads while mixed ("*VARIES*").
size?SelectSizeThe box size.
title?stringThe hint: a short line about the value, added to the accessible description after describedBy.
value?stringThe current value.
variant?SelectVariantThe look.
  • value: the current value; the caller holds it. One that is not in options is listed first.
  • options: the choices as data, { value, label, disabled? }[], in list order.
  • onChange: runs with the picked value. A pick the caller does not take is put back.
  • ariaLabel: the accessible name when no visible label is tied to the control.
  • variant: field (the default) or inline.
  • size: md (the default) or sm.
  • align: start (the default) or end.
  • mixed: the selection holds differing values; shows placeholder.
  • placeholder: what the control reads while mixed. Never a choice.
  • disabled: the native attribute; blocks the list and drops the ink.
  • invalid: the value is refused; sets aria-invalid="true" and the error stroke.
  • describedBy: the id of the help line or the error line (several, space-separated); sets aria-describedby.
  • title: the hint, in the layer's hint box and in the accessible description after describedBy. Never the name, and no native title is rendered. A clipped value is the hint's first line whether or not title is passed.

Usage

When to use

  • The user picks 1 of a known set of values that all fit in a list: a layer, a linetype, a unit.
  • The current value must stay readable while the list is closed, in a form or in a column of values.

When not to use

  • The value is typed rather than picked. Use Field instead.
  • The value is yes or no. Use Checkbox instead.
  • The picks are actions that run at once rather than a value that is held. Use Row in a menu instead.
  • There are 2 or 3 views to switch between, each always visible. Use Tab instead.

Rules

  • rule/select-options-data: When a surface offers a choice, pass the choices as options and the current one as value, because Select renders 0 children and a hand-written <option> never reaches the list. Evidence: single use src/ui/Select.tsx:114, the one place an <option> is rendered, from options. Check: test src/ui/Select.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Select ariaLabel="Layer"><option>0</option></Select>
  • Do: <Select ariaLabel="Layer" value={layer} options={layers.map((name) => ({ value: name, label: name }))} onChange={setLayer} />
  • rule/select-label-bound: When a select is rendered without a visible <label>, pass ariaLabel, because the value is the only text in the box and a screen reader would announce 1 unnamed combo box. Evidence: single use src/ui/Select.tsx:98, the aria-label the prop sets (the palette's choice rows are named this way today). Check: test src/ui/Select.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Select value={layer} options={layers} />
  • Do: <Select ariaLabel="Layer" value={layer} options={layers} onChange={setLayer} />
  • rule/select-off-list-value: When the current value may not be in the list (a layer deleted while an object still names it), pass it as value unchanged and leave the list as it is, because the component lists it as 1 more choice at the top and a control that shows another value would misreport the data. Evidence: single use src/ui/Select.tsx:83, the extra first choice (the palette adds that option by hand today). Check: test src/ui/Select.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Select value={layers.includes(layer) ? layer : layers[0]} options={options} ariaLabel="Layer" />
  • Do: <Select value={layer} options={options} ariaLabel="Layer" onChange={setLayer} />
  • rule/select-mixed-placeholder: When the selected objects hold differing values, pass mixed with a placeholder, because a placeholder added to options becomes 1 selectable choice that writes itself to every object. Evidence: single use src/ui/Select.tsx:109, the placeholder option, hidden and disabled (the palette's *VARIES* rows are the case). Check: test src/ui/Select.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Select value="*VARIES*" options={[{ value: "*VARIES*", label: "*VARIES*" }, ...options]} ariaLabel="Layer" />
  • Do: <Select mixed placeholder="*VARIES*" options={options} ariaLabel="Layer" onChange={setLayer} />
  • rule/select-described-by: When a line of help or an error sits beside a select, give the line an id and pass it as describedBy, and pass invalid while the value is refused, because a line that only sits near the control is read 0 times by a screen reader that lands on it by Tab. Evidence: single use src/ui/Select.tsx:96, the tie Field makes the same way (rule/field-described-by). Check: test src/ui/Select.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Select ariaLabel="Units" value={units} options={all} invalid /><span>Pick a unit the drawing uses.</span>
  • Do: <Select ariaLabel="Units" value={units} options={all} invalid describedBy="units-error" /><span id="units-error">Pick a unit the drawing uses.</span>
  • rule/select-inline-in-rows: When a select sits in a list row beside a label, use variant="inline" with size="sm" and align="end", because a stroked 24px box in each 22px row draws 1 frame per row and the values no longer share an edge. Evidence: measured 20px box in a 22px row and the value ending 16px before the box's edge, in the browser at 1280 wide, 2026-11-11. Check: review src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: <div class="prop-row"><span>Layer</span><Select value={layer} options={options} ariaLabel="Layer" /></div>
  • Do: <div class="prop-row"><span>Layer</span><Select variant="inline" size="sm" align="end" value={layer} options={options} ariaLabel="Layer" /></div>

Content

  • rule/select-option-label-noun: When an option's label is written, use the value's own name as the drawing or the setting spells it (Walls, Continuous, ByLayer), with 0 leading verbs, because the closed control shows the label alone as the current value. Evidence: single use src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:191, the palette's choices: layer and linetype names. Check: review src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: { value: "walls", label: "Move to Walls" }
  • Do: { value: "walls", label: "Walls" }

Anti-slop

  • rule/select-canonical-element: When a surface needs a choice from a list, render Select rather than a raw <select> with its own class or a hand-built listbox, because the replaced class removes the arrow and clips a long value with 0 ellipsis, and a hand-built list loses type-ahead and the phone's picker. Evidence: single use src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:208, which replaced .prop-select (appearance: none, no arrow, a long value cut with no ellipsis). Check: review src/ui/Select.tsx.
  • Don't: <select class="prop-select" onChange={pick}>{options}</select>
  • Do: <Select variant="inline" size="sm" align="end" value={value} options={options} ariaLabel={label} onChange={pick} />

Limits

  • rule/select-label-clip: When an option's label is wider than its box (a 268px label in a 140px box shows 110px of it), let it clip and leave title for what the hint adds, because the value ends in an ellipsis before the arrow and the hint already reads the full label. Evidence: measured 268px label, 110px shown, hint text equal to the full label, in the browser at 1280 wide, 2026-11-11. Check: test src/ui/Select.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Select title={currentLabel} value={value} options={options} ariaLabel="Layer" />
  • Do: <Select value={value} options={options} ariaLabel="Layer" />
  • rule/select-touch-target: When a size="sm" select sits in a list row of 22px, give the row a min-height rather than a fixed height, because under a coarse pointer the box grows from 20px to 24px and a row fixed at 22px would cut it. Evidence: measured 20px box, 24px under the coarse rules, in the browser, 2026-11-11. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: .my-row { height: var(--control-h-row); overflow: hidden }
  • Do: .my-row { min-height: var(--control-h-row) }

Accessibility

Rests on the native <select> element: role, value, the list, type-ahead, the phone's picker and disabled come from the platform. The drawn value and arrow are aria-hidden; assistive tech reads the select itself.

Related

  • Field: when the value is typed rather than picked.
  • Checkbox: when the value is yes or no.
  • Row: when the list is a menu of actions, or a listbox a search field drives.

Tab

Description

It brings one view of a strip to the front: a layout over the drawing or a chat in the assistant, marked selected when it is the one showing.

import { Tab } from "../../../../src/ui/Tab";, source src/ui/Tab.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/button-div, trap/role-button, trap/native-control, trap/current-unmarked, trap/control-height, trap/focus-ring-shape, trap/hover-beats-focus, trap/touch-hover-flash, trap/hover-unguarded, trap/link-wraps-button (n/a: a tab is never a link; the close key is a sibling button, not a nested one), trap/disabled-still-hovers (n/a: a tab has no disabled state).

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — the editor tab (13px type on a 12px inset in the 35px strip, the active one filled with --tab-active, the .08 fill on hover, a hairline between tabs) is measured from the running Cursor 3.27.22 (docs/system/decisions.md), and no registry item ships it. It replaces two hand-built tabs: the raw <button class="layout-tab" role="tab"> of the layout strip, and a Row in a width cell beside a close IconButton in the assistant's header.

Examples

<Tab selected onClick={show}>Model</Tab> — the model-space tab over the drawing.

Real uses, 2 call sites (rg -c "<Tab" src/components → src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:4, src/components/StatusBar.tsx:1):

  • src/components/StatusBar.tsx:76 — LayoutTabs, the editor tabs over the drawing (size="md"): Model, then each layout; selected marks the space in front, title says what the tab switches to.
  • src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:502 — the chat tabs in the assistant's header when more than one chat is open (size="sm"): selected marks the chat in front, onClose closes that chat, closeLabel names it ("Close hello"), title carries the full chat title when the label clips.
  • The menu titles in src/components/MenuBar.tsx stay native buttons: they open menus, a different role.
  • The status bar's drafting toggles in src/components/StatusBar.tsx are Toggle: a drafting toggle is an aria-pressed switch, not a tab.

Example: The tab in front at the active fill, announced as selected. (docs/system/examples/tab/selected.tsx)

import { Tab } from "../../../../src/ui/Tab";

export default function Selected() {
  return <Tab selected>Model</Tab>;
}

State precedence

  • Hinted and Hover: both show. The hint follows the hover after its delay.
  • Hinted and Focused: both show. The hint arrives with the ring, with no delay.
  • Hinted and Pressed: Pressed wins. The press puts the hint away.
  • Hinted and Selected: both show. The tab in front hints like any other.
  • Hinted and Closable: both show. The close key shows its own hint (closeLabel) when the pointer or the focus is on it.
  • Hover and Selected: Selected wins. The active fill stays under the pointer; hover adds nothing to the tab in front.
  • Hover and Focused: both show. The ring stays drawn over the hover fill.
  • Selected and Focused: both show. The ring draws around the active fill.
  • Pressed and Focused: both show. The ring stays drawn while the tab is held down.
  • Closable and Selected: both show. Every closable tab keeps its close key, in front or behind.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
The pointer enters or leavesinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)background-color, colorThe fill and ink change at once: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] rule removes the transition.
The tab comes to the front or goes behindinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)background-color, colorThe fill and ink change at once, by the same rule.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
children?ElementThe tab's label.
closeLabel?stringThe close key's accessible name and tooltip.
onClick?((event: MouseEvent) => void)Runs on click: the caller brings this tab to the front.
onClose?(() => void)Draws a trailing close key that runs this, and never onClick.
selected?booleanThe tab in front: the active fill, the full ink, and aria-selected="true".
size?TabSizeThe size.
title?stringThe hint: what the tab switches to.
  • selected: the tab in front; sets aria-selected="true" (and "false" otherwise) and the selected fill of its size.
  • size: sm or md; defaults to md.
  • title: the hint, shown in the layer's hint box and tied to the tab as its accessible description (aria-describedby): what the tab switches to. It is never the name, and no native title attribute is rendered. A title equal to the label draws no hint and adds no description. A clipped label needs no title: the hint shows the full label by itself, with the title on a second line when it says more.
  • onClick: runs on click; the caller brings this tab to the front.
  • onClose: draws the trailing close key and runs when it is clicked; the tab's onClick does not run.
  • closeLabel: the close key's accessible name and tooltip; defaults to "Close".
  • children: the tab's label.

Usage

When to use

  • Several views share one area and one shows at a time: the model space and the layouts over the drawing, the open chats in the assistant.
  • The view in front must be marked for a screen reader as well as the eye.

When not to use

  • The control runs an action rather than showing a view. Use Button instead.
  • The item is one band of a full-width list (a layer, a menu item, a command). Use Row instead.
  • The control flips a setting on and off (a drafting toggle). Use IconButton with selected instead.
  • The label is a short fact with no view behind it. Use Chip instead.

Rules

  • rule/tab-selected-marked: When a strip has a tab in front, pass selected on it, because the fill alone is colour and a screen reader needs aria-selected="true" to hear which view shows. Evidence: app 2/2 strips mark the tab in front, src/components/StatusBar.tsx:57 and src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:434. Check: test src/ui/Tab.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tab onClick={show}>Model</Tab> for the tab whose view is showing.
  • Do: <Tab selected onClick={show}>Model</Tab>
  • rule/tab-in-tablist: When tabs are rendered, place them in 1 container carrying role="tablist" and an aria-label, because a tab role outside a tablist is announced without its strip and its position. Evidence: app 2/2 strips, src/components/StatusBar.tsx:54 and src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:499. Check: review src/components/StatusBar.tsx.
  • Don't: <div class="editor-tabs"><Tab selected>Model</Tab></div>
  • Do: <div class="editor-tabs" role="tablist" aria-label="Layouts"><Tab selected>Model</Tab></div>
  • rule/tab-close-sibling: When a tab can be closed, pass onClose rather than putting a button in the tab's children, because a <button> cannot nest a <button> and Tab renders the close key as a sibling. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:434, the one closable strip. Check: test src/ui/Tab.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tab onClick={show}>hello<IconButton icon="close" title="Close hello" onClick={close} /></Tab>
  • Do: <Tab onClick={show} onClose={close} closeLabel="Close hello">hello</Tab>

Content

  • rule/tab-close-label-names: When onClose is passed, pass closeLabel as "Close" plus the tab's label ("Close hello"), because 2 close keys both named "Close" in one strip cannot be told apart by a screen reader. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:434. Check: review src/components/AssistantPane.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tab onClose={close}>hello</Tab> in a strip of 2 closable tabs.
  • Do: <Tab onClose={close} closeLabel="Close hello">hello</Tab>

Anti-slop

  • rule/tab-canonical-element: When a surface needs a tab, render Tab rather than a raw <button role="tab"> with its own class or a Row in a width cell, because the 2 replaced recipes painted 2 different selected fills and only 1 of them set aria-selected. Evidence: app 2/2 hand-built tabs replaced (.layout-tab and .assistant-tab-row), src/components/StatusBar.tsx:57 and src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:434. Check: review src/ui/Tab.tsx.
  • Don't: <button class="layout-tab is-active" role="tab">Model</button>
  • Do: <Tab selected>Model</Tab>

Limits

  • rule/tab-label-limit: When an sm tab's label runs past 18 characters, pass the whole label as the children and leave the shortening to the tab, because the tab clips at max-width: 18ch with an ellipsis (the 20-character "Summarise the layers" shows as "Summarise the la…") and shows the full label in its hint by itself, while a label cut by the caller has no full text anywhere. Evidence: measured 111.6px clipped sm tab at 1280px, src/ui/ui.css:981. Check: test src/ui/Tab.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tab size="sm">{title.slice(0, 16) + "…"}</Tab> — the cut label has no full text anywhere.
  • Do: <Tab size="sm">Summarise the layers</Tab>
  • rule/tab-md-label-limit: When an md tab's label runs past 24 characters, pass the whole label as the children and leave the shortening to the tab, because the tab clips at max-width: 24ch with an ellipsis and shows the full label in its hint by itself, and uncapped the 56-character "A1 Ground floor general arrangement plan, sheet 12 of 40" draws a 357.8px tab that pushes the other layouts out of the strip. Evidence: measured 168.2px clipped md tab at 1280px, src/ui/ui.css:970. Check: test src/ui/Tab.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tab title="A1 Ground floor general arrangement plan, sheet 12 of 40">A1 Ground floor…</Tab> — the label a screen reader hears is the cut one.
  • Do: <Tab>A1 Ground floor general arrangement plan, sheet 12 of 40</Tab>
  • rule/tab-touch-target: When sm tabs are laid out in a pane header, leave the header room for a 24px tab, because under a coarse pointer the 22px tab grows to the 24px control height (it clips its own overflow for the ellipsis, so it cannot take an overhanging target) and a header fixed at 22px would cut it. Evidence: measured 22px sm tab, 24px under a coarse pointer, src/ui/ui.css:1165. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: .my-head { height: var(--control-h-row); overflow: hidden }
  • Do: .my-head { min-height: var(--control-h-button); align-items: center }

Accessibility

Rests on the native <button> element with role="tab": Enter and Space and focus come from the platform. Every tab stays in the tab order; the strip has no arrow-key handler, so a tab is reached by Tab, not by the arrow keys. The caller owns the tablist container, and no tabpanel is wired (aria-controls is not set).

Related

  • Row: when the item is one band of a full-width list rather than one view of a strip.
  • IconButton: the close key a closable tab draws; and the pick for an on/off toggle.
  • Button: when the control runs an action rather than showing a view.

TextArea

Description

It takes several lines of text, grows to hold them up to a limit, and hands every edit back to the caller, who owns the text.

import { TextArea } from "../../../../src/ui/TextArea";, source src/ui/TextArea.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/native-control, trap/control-height, trap/field-label, trap/label-unbound, trap/field-input-type, trap/field-affix-focus (n/a: no affix part), trap/field-form-enter, trap/field-error-link, trap/field-error-timing, trap/field-keeps-input, trap/touch-input-zoom, trap/touch-autofocus, trap/focus-ring-shape, trap/hover-beats-focus, trap/disabled-still-hovers, trap/overflow-scrollbar.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — a native <textarea> in Field's measured recipe (the hairline stroke, the focus edge, 13px type; docs/system/decisions.md), and no registry item ships it.

<TextArea value={notes()} onInput={setNotes} ariaLabel="Notes" /> — a notes field: two lines tall when empty, growing to eight.

  • src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:1011 — the composer's editor: variant="bare" inside the card, two rows growing to nine, the combobox of the slash list while that list shows.

import { TextArea } from "../../../../src/ui/TextArea";

export default function InAssistantPane() {
  return (
    <div class="assistant-composer">
      <TextArea
        variant="bare"
        rows={2}
        maxRows={9}
        value="Draw a circle at 20,20"
        placeholder="Ask, or / for commands"
        ariaLabel="Ask the assistant"
        onInput={() => undefined}

Variants

variant

  • field: the form control, with Field's stroke, fill, padding and type; one line is exactly a Field's 24px. The default. Used at 0 call sites.
  • bare: no stroke, no fill, no padding and no ring, with the type of the element around it; for an editor inside a card that draws those itself. Used at 0 call sites (the assistant's composer is planned).

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by

Example: Refused text at the error stroke, with the line that says why. (docs/system/examples/textarea/invalid.tsx)

import { TextArea } from "../../../../src/ui/TextArea";

export default function Invalid() {
  return (
    <div>
      <TextArea value="LINE 0,0 10" ariaLabel="Script" invalid describedBy="script-error" spellcheck={false} onInput={() => undefined} />
      <span id="script-error">Line 1 ends before its second point.</span>
    </div>
  );
}

State precedence

  • Focused and Hover: Focused wins. The focus stroke and the ring stay under the pointer.
  • Growing and Scrolling: Not applicable: the text fits within maxRows lines or it does not.
  • Growing and Focused: both show. The box grows under the caret with the focus stroke drawn.
  • Scrolling and Focused: both show. The capped box keeps its focus stroke while its text scrolls.
  • Invalid and Focused: both show. On field the stroke keeps the error ink and the ring draws one line inside it.
  • Invalid and Hover: Invalid wins. The error stroke stays under the pointer.
  • Invalid and Growing: both show. Text past a caller's limit keeps growing the box inside the error stroke; nothing is cut.
  • Invalid and Disabled: Disabled wins. The caller clears invalid before it locks text nobody can correct.
  • Disabled and Hover: Disabled wins. A disabled control takes no caret and no ring.
  • Disabled and Scrolling: both show. Locked text past the cap can still be scrolled and read.
  • Composing and Focused: both show. The focus stroke stays while the input method holds the keys.
  • Composing and Growing: both show. The box grows as composed text is committed.

ariaLabel?stringThe accessible name when no visible <label> is tied to the control.
autocomplete?stringThe native autofill hint; off for text no form should remember.
autocompleteKind?AutocompleteKindA combobox: what its list does with the typed text (aria-autocomplete).
autoFocus?booleanFocus the control when it mounts.
controls?stringA combobox: the id of its list (aria-controls).
describedBy?stringThe id of the help line or the error line beside the control (several, space-separated): sets aria-describedby.
disabled?booleanBlocks typing and drops the ink to the disabled step.
expanded?booleanA combobox: whether its list is showing now (aria-expanded).
invalid?booleanThe text is refused: sets aria-invalid and, on field, the error stroke.
maxRows?numberThe most lines it grows to before it scrolls.
onInput?((value: string) => void)Runs on every edit with the new text.
onKeyDown?((event: KeyboardEvent) => void)A key went down in the control, outside an input method's composition.
onPaste?((event: ClipboardEvent) => void)Something was pasted: the caller may take what is not text (a picture) from the clipboard.
placeholder?stringThe placeholder.
ref?((el: HTMLTextAreaElement) => void)Hands the element to the caller, to focus it or to place the caret.
role?"combobox"The text drives a list of matches and keeps the keyboard: combobox.
rows?numberThe fewest lines it shows.
spellcheck?booleanWhether the platform's spelling checker runs.
title?stringThe hint: a short line about the text, added to the accessible description after describedBy.
value?stringThe current text.
variant?TextAreaVariantThe look.
  • value: the current text; the caller holds it. It is written to the element only when it differs from what is typed, so a composition is never restarted.
  • onInput: runs on every edit with the new text.
  • placeholder: an example of the text; never the only name.
  • ariaLabel: the accessible name when no visible label is tied to the control.
  • variant: field (the default) or bare.
  • rows: the fewest lines shown; defaults to 2.
  • maxRows: the most lines it grows to before it scrolls; defaults to 8.
  • disabled: the native attribute; blocks typing and drops the ink.
  • invalid: the text is refused; sets aria-invalid="true" and, on field, the error stroke.
  • describedBy: the id of the help line or the error line (several, space-separated); sets aria-describedby.
  • title: the hint, in the layer's hint box and in the accessible description after describedBy. Never the name, and no native title is rendered.
  • autoFocus: focuses the control when it mounts.
  • autocomplete: the native autofill hint; unset leaves it to the platform.
  • spellcheck: switches the platform's spelling checker; unset leaves it to the platform.
  • onKeyDown: a key went down outside an input method's composition; the caller may preventDefault it.
  • onPaste: something was pasted; the caller may take what is not text.
  • ref: hands the element to the caller, to focus it or to place the caret.
  • role: combobox, while the text drives a list of matches and keeps the keyboard (the composer's slash list).
  • expanded: a combobox's list is showing (aria-expanded).
  • controls: the id of a combobox's list (aria-controls).
  • activeDescendant: the id of the option the arrow keys are on (aria-activedescendant); unset when none is.
  • autocompleteKind: what the list does with the typed text (aria-autocomplete): list, inline, both or none.

Usage

When to use

  • The user writes more than 1 line: a message to the assistant, a note on a layer, a block of script.
  • The text's length is not known ahead, and the control should take the room the text needs before it scrolls.

When not to use

  • The text is 1 line: a name, a coordinate, a keyword. Use Field instead.
  • The value is picked from a list. Use Select instead.
  • The text is a fact to read rather than to edit. Use Chip instead.

Rules

  • rule/textarea-label-bound: When a text area is rendered without a visible <label>, pass ariaLabel, because a placeholder disappears at the first character and leaves 1 unnamed text box. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:976, the composer's editor, named "Ask the assistant" with a placeholder beside it. Check: test src/ui/TextArea.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <TextArea placeholder="Ask, or / for commands" value={draft()} onInput={setDraft} />
  • Do: <TextArea ariaLabel="Ask the assistant" placeholder="Ask, or / for commands" value={draft()} onInput={setDraft} />
  • rule/textarea-rows-not-height: When a text area needs a smallest or a largest size, pass rows and maxRows rather than a height, min-height or max-height in a stylesheet, because the component sets the height itself from the measured text on every edit and a second height fights it by 1 line or more. Evidence: single use src/ui/TextArea.tsx:113, the one place the height is set. Check: test src/ui/TextArea.test.tsx.
  • Don't: .my-notes .ui-textarea { min-height: 64px; max-height: 240px }
  • Do: <TextArea rows={2} maxRows={9} ariaLabel="Notes" value={notes()} onInput={setNotes} />
  • rule/textarea-enter-in-keydown: When Enter sends the text, handle it in onKeyDown and call preventDefault, leaving Shift+Enter to break the line, because onKeyDown hears 0 keys while an input method is composing and a handler on a wrapper would send a half-composed word. Evidence: single use src/ui/TextArea.tsx:191, the composition guard. Check: test src/ui/TextArea.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <div onKeyDown={(e) => e.key === "Enter" && send()}><TextArea ariaLabel="Ask" value={draft()} onInput={setDraft} /></div>
  • Do: <TextArea ariaLabel="Ask" value={draft()} onInput={setDraft} onKeyDown={(e) => { if (e.key === "Enter" && !e.shiftKey) { e.preventDefault(); send(); } }} />
  • rule/textarea-bare-card-focus: When variant="bare" is used, give the card around it the focus cue with :focus-within, because the bare editor draws 0 rings of its own and a keyboard user would otherwise see no focus at all. Evidence: single use src/ui/ui.css:877, the bare recipe, which drops the ring. Check: review src/assistant.css.
  • Don't: <div class="card"><TextArea variant="bare" ariaLabel="Ask" /></div> with no .card:focus-within rule.
  • Do: .card:focus-within { border-color: var(--composer-border-active) } around <TextArea variant="bare" ariaLabel="Ask" />
  • rule/textarea-described-by: When a line of help, a count or an error sits beside a text area, give the line an id and pass it as describedBy, and pass invalid while the text is refused, because a line that only sits near the control is read 0 times by a screen reader that lands on it by Tab. Evidence: single use src/ui/TextArea.tsx:167, the tie Field makes the same way (rule/field-described-by). Check: test src/ui/TextArea.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <TextArea ariaLabel="Ask" invalid /><div>120 characters too long to send</div>
  • Do: <TextArea ariaLabel="Ask" invalid describedBy="ask-over" /><div id="ask-over">120 characters too long to send</div>
  • rule/textarea-combobox-while-listed: When a text area drives a list of matches for part of what is typed, pass role="combobox" with expanded, controls and activeDescendant only while the list shows, and drop all 4 when it goes, because a multi-line text box that always says it is a combobox is announced as 1 on every focus, and its arrow keys are then expected to walk a list that is not there. Evidence: app 5/5 combobox props defined together in src/ui/TextArea.tsx. Check: test src/ui/TextArea.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <TextArea ariaLabel="Ask the assistant" role="combobox" expanded={false} value={draft()} onInput={setDraft} /> on a composer with no list open.
  • Do: <TextArea ariaLabel="Ask the assistant" role={listed() ? "combobox" : undefined} expanded={listed() ? true : undefined} controls={listed() ? "slash-list" : undefined} activeDescendant={listed() ? activeId() : undefined} value={draft()} onInput={setDraft} />

Content

  • rule/textarea-placeholder-example: When a placeholder is written, show in 2 to 6 words what goes here or what the control takes (Ask, or / for commands) and put a rule the user must keep in mind in a line tied by describedBy, because the placeholder is gone at the first character. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:976, the composer's two placeholders. Check: review src/components/AssistantPane.tsx.
  • Don't: <TextArea ariaLabel="Ask" placeholder="Messages must be under 8,000 characters and may not be empty" />
  • Do: <TextArea ariaLabel="Ask the assistant" placeholder="Ask, or / for commands" />

Anti-slop

  • rule/textarea-canonical-element: When a surface needs multi-line text, render TextArea rather than a raw <textarea> with its own class and its own grow function, because the hand-built one fixes its limits in pixels (64 and 240) where the type size they were counted from can change, and every copy re-solves composition and growth. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:88, the composer's own grow. Check: review src/ui/TextArea.tsx.
  • Don't: <textarea class="assistant-input" rows={1} onInput={(e) => grow(e.currentTarget)} />
  • Do: <TextArea variant="bare" rows={2} maxRows={9} ariaLabel="Ask the assistant" value={draft()} onInput={setDraft} />

Limits

  • rule/textarea-max-rows: When text may run past 8 lines, leave maxRows at 8 or set it to the lines the surface can spare (9 in the composer), because past the cap the box stops and scrolls, and a cap the surface cannot hold pushes the send key off the screen. Evidence: measured 72px box, 230px scrollHeight, overflow-y: auto, in the browser at 1280 wide, 2026-11-11. Check: test src/ui/TextArea.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <TextArea maxRows={200} ariaLabel="Ask" /> above a send key.
  • Do: <TextArea maxRows={9} ariaLabel="Ask the assistant" />
  • rule/textarea-one-row-field: When a text area sits on a row with a Field, pass rows={1}, because 1 line of the field variant measures the Field's 24px and the default 2 lines measure 40px. Evidence: measured 24px at rows={1} beside a 24px Field and 40px at the default, in the browser, 2026-11-11. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: <div class="form-row"><Field ariaLabel="Name" /><TextArea ariaLabel="Note" /></div>
  • Do: <div class="form-row"><Field ariaLabel="Name" /><TextArea rows={1} ariaLabel="Note" /></div>

Accessibility

Rests on the native <textarea> element: typing, selection, IME, undo and disabled come from the platform. The height is paint: assistive tech reads the whole text whatever shows.

Keyboard

KeyWhere focus isEffectFocus afterChecked by
TabThe control, in document order.Moves focus in; on field the focus stroke and ring draw. Tab never types a tab character, so the keyboard is never trapped.On the control.by hand
Tab (disabled)A disabled control is skipped.Focus moves past it.On the next control.by hand
EnterThe focused control.Breaks the line and the box grows by one, unless the caller's onKeyDown prevents it (to send).Stays on the control.test
Enter (composing)The focused control, mid-composition.Confirms the input method's candidate; onKeyDown is not called.Stays on the control.test
ArrowUp / ArrowDown, PageUp / PageDownThe focused control.Move the caret; past the cap the text scrolls to keep it in view.Stays on the control.by hand
ArrowUp / ArrowDown, Enter (combobox)The focused control, while its list shows.The caller's onKeyDown moves activeDescendant through the list or runs the active option, and prevents the caret's move; the control moves no focus.Stays on the control.by hand

Related

  • Field: when the text is one line.
  • Select: when the value is picked rather than written.
  • Button: when the text is sent by a control beside it.
  • IconButton: the send key beside a composer's editor.
  • Tooltip: the hint box a title shows in; never wrap a text area in one.

Toggle

Description

It switches one setting on or off in place, under a name that never changes, and says which it is through its pressed state.

import { Toggle } from "../../../../src/ui/Toggle";, source src/ui/Toggle.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/button-div, trap/role-button, trap/native-control, trap/button-icon-name, trap/icon-optical-size, trap/icon-optical-align, trap/control-height, trap/focus-ring-shape, trap/hover-beats-focus, trap/disabled-still-hovers, trap/touch-hover-flash, trap/hover-unguarded, trap/touch-tap-highlight, trap/color-only-status, trap/toggle-switch-submit (n/a: type="button", a toggle never submits), trap/toggle-indeterminate (n/a: a toggle is on or off; a value that can be mixed is a Checkbox), trap/weight-shift (n/a: on and off are one weight, so a word never changes width).

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — a native <button aria-pressed> drawn from the layer's tokens; the two faces are the app's own measured ones (the layer list's state keys in src/styles.css and the status bar's drafting toggles in src/chrome.css, moved here value for value on 2026-11-11), and the glyphs are the app's own src/icons.ts paths.

Examples

<Toggle size="sm" tone="info" icon="layer.thawed" iconOn="layer.frozen" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" hint={frozen() ? "Thaw" : "Freeze"} pressed={frozen()} onChange={setFrozen} /> — a layer's freeze key: one name, the state in the glyph and aria-pressed, the action in the hint.

Real uses, 4 call sites (rg -c "<Toggle" src/components → src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:3, src/components/StatusBar.tsx:1):

  • src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:127 — a layer row's on key: glyph, sm, tone="absent" (off is the state that explains a missing layer).
  • src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:137 — the same row's frozen key: tone="info".
  • src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:147 — the same row's locked key: tone="caution".
  • src/components/StatusBar.tsx:171 — each of the status bar's 11 drafting settings: text, sm, the function key as shortcut, the hint above the bar, in a toolbar that is one Tab stop.
