Variants

variant

  • glyph: an icon that changes with the state (icon off, iconOn on), in the ink its tone picks; the default. Used at 3 call sites (a layer row's on, frozen and locked keys).
  • text: a short word in capitals; on, the full ink over a hairline rule in the on-colour. Used at 1 call site (the status bar's drafting settings, 11 rendered).

Example: The glyph face: an icon for each state, the state in the glyph and its ink. (docs/system/examples/toggle/variant-glyph.tsx)

import { Toggle } from "../../../../src/ui/Toggle";

export default function VariantGlyph() {
  return <Toggle variant="glyph" pressed icon="layer.unlocked" iconOn="layer.locked" tone="caution" ariaLabel="Outline locked" hint="Unlock" />;
}

Example: The text face: a word in capitals, on with the full ink over the on-colour rule. (docs/system/examples/toggle/variant-text.tsx)

import { Toggle } from "../../../../src/ui/Toggle";

export default function VariantText() {
  return (
    <Toggle variant="text" pressed ariaLabel="Grid" hint="Grid" shortcut="F7">
      Grid
    </Toggle>
  );
}

size

  • sm: the cell of a dense surface. A glyph is 20px wide at the 22px row height with the 12px glyph; a word is 11px type as tall as the line that holds it (--ui-toggle-line, the row height when nothing sets it). Used at 4 call sites (all of them).
  • md: the 24px control beside a field or an icon button, with the 14px glyph or 12px type; the default. Used at 0 call sites: the size for a toggle outside a list row or a bar, which no surface has yet.

Example: The 20 by 22 cell of a list row, with the 12px glyph. (docs/system/examples/toggle/size-sm.tsx)

import { Toggle } from "../../../../src/ui/Toggle";

export default function SizeSm() {
  return <Toggle size="sm" pressed={false} icon="layer.thawed" iconOn="layer.frozen" tone="info" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" hint="Freeze" />;
}

Example: The 24px control, with the 14px glyph. (docs/system/examples/toggle/size-md.tsx)

import { Toggle } from "../../../../src/ui/Toggle";

export default function SizeMd() {
  return <Toggle size="md" pressed={false} icon="eye-off" iconOn="eye" ariaLabel="Preview" hint="Show the preview" />;
}

tone

  • neutral: on is the full ink (--text) over the quiet one; the default, and the only tone of a text face. Used at 1 call site (the status bar's settings).
  • absent: on is the ordinary state and stays at the glyph ink; off is the one to notice and takes the ink. Used at 1 call site (a layer's on key).
  • info: on is a fact to notice. Used at 1 call site (a layer's frozen key).
  • caution: on blocks something. Used at 1 call site (a layer's locked key).

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
Rest (off)pressed is false.Press it, or Tab to it and press Space or Enter, to ask for on.The off glyph (icon), or the word with no rule under it; aria-pressed="false".test
Pressed (on)The caller passes pressed.Press it to ask for off.The on glyph (iconOn), or the 1px rule under the word; aria-pressed="true". No fill in either state.test

FocusedKeyboard focus arrives by Tab, or by an arrow key in a group that roves.Space or Enter asks for the other state.The 1px ring in the focus ink at offset -1, on the cell's edge.by hand

Example: The same toggle on: the on glyph in the full ink, no fill, announced pressed. (docs/system/examples/toggle/pressed.tsx)

import { Toggle } from "../../../../src/ui/Toggle";

export default function Pressed() {
  return <Toggle pressed icon="eye-off" iconOn="eye" ariaLabel="Preview" hint="Hide the preview" />;
}

Example: A blocked toggle at the disabled ink, still focusable, saying why. (docs/system/examples/toggle/disabled.tsx)

import { Toggle } from "../../../../src/ui/Toggle";

/** Disabled, and still reachable: the hint says what a press would do and `description` why it cannot. */
export default function Disabled() {
  return <Toggle pressed={false} disabled size="sm" tone="info" icon="layer.thawed" iconOn="layer.frozen" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" hint="Freeze" description="The current layer cannot be frozen" />;
}

State precedence

  • Pressed and Hover: both show. The on ink stays under the pointer; hover adds only the fill.
  • Rest and Hover: both show. The fill arrives, and the quiet ink steps to the full ink; an absent toggle that is off keeps its own ink, which is the state.
  • Held and Hover: Held wins. The .14 fill replaces the .08 one while the pointer is down.
  • Held and Pressed: both show. The on face stays while the fill is held.
  • Focused and Hover: both show. The ring stays drawn while the fill steps.
  • Focused and Pressed: both show. The ring is on the cell's edge and the state is in the face.
  • Focused and Held: both show. The ring stays drawn while the toggle is held down.
  • Hinted and Held: Held wins. The press puts the hint away.
  • Hinted and Hover: both show. The hint follows the hover after its delay.
  • Hinted and Focused: both show. The hint arrives with the ring, with no delay.
  • Hinted and Pressed: both show. The hint says what a press does now, in either state.
  • Hinted and Disabled: both show. A disabled toggle still says what it is for, and why it is blocked when it has a description.
  • Disabled and Hover: Disabled wins. No fill and no ink change under the pointer.
  • Disabled and Held: Disabled wins. No fill, and the press is refused.
  • Disabled and Pressed: both show. The on glyph or the rule stays, at the disabled ink, and aria-pressed still says the state.
  • Disabled and Focused: both show. A disabled toggle takes focus and the ring, so a keyboard user can reach its hint; Enter and Space do nothing.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
The pointer enters, presses or leaves, or the state changesinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-standard)background-color, colorThe fill and the ink change at once: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] * rule removes the transition. The glyph and the rule swap at once in every setting.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
pressedbooleanWhether the setting is on.
ariaLabel?stringThe fixed accessible name: the setting, not the action ("Outline frozen").
children?ElementThe word of a text face ("Grid").
description?stringA second line under the hint and the toggle's accessible description: why it is disabled.
disabled?booleanBlocks the press and drops the face to the disabled ink.
hint?stringThe hint, for the eye: what a press does now ("Thaw"), or the full name of a terse face.
icon?stringThe glyph shown while off, and while on when iconOn is not given: an id from ../icons.ts.
iconOn?stringThe glyph shown while on.
onChange?((pressed: boolean) => void)Runs on a press, with the state the press asks for.
onClick?((event: MouseEvent) => void)Runs on click, before onChange.
placement?TooltipPlacementThe side the hint prefers; it flips by itself when that side has no room.
shortcut?stringThe shortcut that flips the same setting, as the user reads it ("F9"): a key cap in the hint and aria-keyshortcuts on the button.
size?ToggleSizeThe box.
tabIndex?numberThe toggle's place in the Tab order, for a group that is one Tab stop.
tone?ToggleToneThe ink of the state worth noticing.
variant?ToggleVariantThe face.
  • pressed: whether the setting is on; the caller holds it. Sets aria-pressed.
  • onChange: runs with the state a press asks for. The toggle then shows what pressed says, so a change the caller refuses does not stay drawn.
  • onClick: runs on click, before onChange; a disabled toggle never fires either.
  • variant: the face; defaults to glyph.
  • icon: the glyph shown while off (and while on, when iconOn is not given): an id from src/icons.ts.
  • iconOn: the glyph shown while on.
  • tone: which state is the one to notice, and its ink; defaults to neutral. A text face is always neutral.
  • size: the box; defaults to md.
  • ariaLabel: the fixed accessible name: the setting, never the action. Required on a glyph; on a text face, the full name when the word is short for it.
  • hint: the layer's hint, for the eye only: what a press does now, or the full name of a terse word. It is not exposed to assistive tech, which has the name and the state. No native title attribute is rendered.
  • shortcut: the shortcut that flips the same setting, as the user reads it (F9): a key cap in the hint and aria-keyshortcuts on the button.
  • description: a second line under the hint, tied to the toggle as its accessible description (aria-describedby): why it is disabled.
  • placement: the side the hint prefers (top, bottom); it flips by itself when that side has no room.
  • disabled: blocks the press and drops the face to the disabled ink. It sets aria-disabled="true", never the native disabled, so the toggle stays in the Tab order and its hint still shows.
  • tabIndex: the toggle's place in the Tab order, for a group that is one Tab stop. Unset writes no attribute, so a container that roves through the element (rovingBand) is not undone.
  • children: the word of a text face.

Usage

When to use

  • A setting of the thing in front of the person is on or off and takes effect the moment it is pressed: a layer is frozen, the grid is shown.
  • Several such settings repeat down a list or along a bar, most of them on, where a fill on each would be a row of fills.

When not to use

  • The value is applied with a form, or can be mixed across several objects. Use Checkbox instead.
  • The glyph runs an action, opens a menu or folds a region. Use IconButton instead.
  • One switch on a tool bar should read as lit while on, with a fill. Use IconButton with selected instead.
  • The control brings one view of several to the front. Use Tab instead.

Rules

  • rule/toggle-name-fixed: When a toggle is rendered, pass 1 ariaLabel that names the setting and is the same string in both states, and put the action in hint, because aria-pressed already says the state, and a name that flips between Freeze and Thaw is heard as 2 different buttons. Evidence: app 3/3 layer state keys, src/components/LayersPanel.tsx. Check: test src/ui/Toggle.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Toggle icon="layer.thawed" iconOn="layer.frozen" ariaLabel={frozen() ? "Thaw Outline" : "Freeze Outline"} pressed={frozen()} />
  • Do: <Toggle icon="layer.thawed" iconOn="layer.frozen" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" hint={frozen() ? "Thaw" : "Freeze"} pressed={frozen()} />
  • rule/toggle-state-in-face: When a glyph toggle is rendered, pass 2 icons (icon for off, iconOn for on), because the toggle draws no fill at rest and the ink alone would carry the state by colour only. Evidence: app 3/3 layer state keys pass both, src/components/LayersPanel.tsx. Check: review src/components/LayersPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: <Toggle icon="layer.locked" tone="caution" ariaLabel="Outline locked" pressed={locked()} />
  • Do: <Toggle icon="layer.unlocked" iconOn="layer.locked" tone="caution" ariaLabel="Outline locked" pressed={locked()} />
  • rule/toggle-owns-nothing: When onChange runs, set the caller's own value from its argument (or refuse it), because the toggle draws from pressed after every press and keeps 0 state of its own. Evidence: single use src/ui/Toggle.tsx:97, the aria-pressed the prop sets. Check: test src/ui/Toggle.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Toggle icon="eye-off" iconOn="eye" ariaLabel="Preview" pressed={false} onChange={() => save()} />
  • Do: <Toggle icon="eye-off" iconOn="eye" ariaLabel="Preview" pressed={preview()} onChange={setPreview} />
  • rule/toggle-tone-meaning: When a tone is passed, pick it by which state the person must notice (absent for off, info or caution for on) and pass 1 tone per setting across the whole list, because the tone is the only colour in the column and a tone picked for looks makes 2 rows of the same setting read as different things. Evidence: app 3/3 layer state keys, each with its own tone on every row, src/components/LayersPanel.tsx. Check: review src/components/LayersPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: <Toggle tone="caution" icon="layer.off" iconOn="layer.on" ariaLabel="Outline on" pressed={on()} /> — on is the ordinary state, and it would be drawn as a warning on every row.
  • Do: <Toggle tone="absent" icon="layer.off" iconOn="layer.on" ariaLabel="Outline on" pressed={on()} />
  • rule/toggle-group-one-stop: When more than 3 toggles stand in one bar, give the bar role="toolbar" with a name and make it 1 Tab stop (the container sets each tabIndex; the arrows, Home and End move), because 11 Tab stops in the status bar stand between the drawing and everything after it. Evidence: single use src/components/StatusBar.tsx:168, the toolbar that roves its 11 toggles. Check: review src/components/StatusBar.tsx.
  • Don't: <div class="status-toggles"><Toggle variant="text" pressed={grid()}>Grid</Toggle>…</div> with 11 Tab stops.
  • Do: <div class="status-toggles" role="toolbar" aria-label="Drafting settings" ref={(el) => rovingBand(el, "button")}>…</div>
  • rule/toggle-no-native-title: When a toggle is styled or wrapped, add 0 hints of its own (no title attribute set from outside, no Tooltip around it), because the component already shows hint in the layer's hint box and a second hint stacks on the first. Evidence: app 38/38 toggles in the running shell render no title attribute, measured in the browser 2026-11-11. Check: test src/ui/Toggle.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tooltip text="Thaw"><Toggle icon="layer.thawed" iconOn="layer.frozen" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" pressed /></Tooltip>
  • Do: <Toggle icon="layer.thawed" iconOn="layer.frozen" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" hint="Thaw" pressed />
  • rule/toggle-disabled-reason: When a toggle is disabled by something the person can change, pass the reason as description in 1 short sentence, because the disabled toggle stays focusable for exactly this, and hint is not exposed to a screen reader. Evidence: single use src/ui/Toggle.tsx:91, the description tied to the button. Check: test src/ui/Toggle.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Toggle disabled icon="layer.thawed" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" hint="The current layer cannot be frozen" pressed={false} />
  • Do: <Toggle disabled icon="layer.thawed" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" hint="Freeze" description="The current layer cannot be frozen" pressed={false} />

Content

  • rule/toggle-label-setting: When ariaLabel is written, name the setting as a noun phrase of 1 to 4 words that is true while the toggle is pressed (Outline frozen, Snap mode), in sentence case, because it is read with "pressed" or "not pressed" after it, and a verb there reads as a command. Evidence: app 14/14 toggle names in the layer list and the status bar, src/components/StatusBar.tsx. Check: review src/components/StatusBar.tsx.
  • Don't: ariaLabel="Freeze the layer"
  • Do: ariaLabel="Outline frozen"
  • rule/toggle-text-short: When a text face is written, pass 1 word of at most 6 letters and the full name as ariaLabel and hint, because the bar holds 11 of them on one line at 1280 wide and the capitals are tracked. Evidence: app 11/11 status toggles ("Grid" to "OTrack", 2 to 6 letters), src/components/StatusBar.tsx. Check: review src/components/StatusBar.tsx.
  • Don't: <Toggle variant="text" pressed={on()}>Object snap tracking</Toggle>
  • Do: <Toggle variant="text" ariaLabel="Object snap tracking" hint="Object snap tracking" pressed={on()}>OTrack</Toggle>

Anti-slop

  • rule/toggle-canonical-element: When a surface needs an on-off key, render Toggle rather than a raw <button aria-pressed> with its own class, because the 2 replaced families (.toggle, .status-toggle) each carried their own hover, ring and state inks and neither had a disabled state or a touch target. Evidence: app 4/4 raw aria-pressed buttons in src/components/LayersPanel.tsx and src/components/StatusBar.tsx before 2026-11-11. Check: lint node scripts/check-system.mjs --root ..
  • Don't: <button class="toggle is-frozen" type="button" aria-pressed="true" aria-label="Outline frozen">…</button>
  • Do: <Toggle size="sm" tone="info" icon="layer.thawed" iconOn="layer.frozen" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" pressed />
  • rule/toggle-no-fill: When a toggle should look on, pass pressed and add 0 background rules of the surface's own, because the glyph, the ink or the rule already says so, and 1 fill per pressed key turns a list where nearly every row is on into a column of fills. Evidence: measured 0 fills at rest on the 38 toggles of the running shell, in both states, 2026-11-11. Check: test src/ui/recipe.test.ts.
  • Don't: .layer-toggles .ui-toggle[aria-pressed="true"] { background: var(--fill-active) }
  • Do: <Toggle tone="info" icon="layer.thawed" iconOn="layer.frozen" ariaLabel="Outline frozen" pressed />

Limits

  • rule/toggle-touch-target: When 2 sm glyph toggles sit side by side, keep at least 4px between them under a coarse pointer, because each 20px by 22px cell keeps its drawn size there and takes a 24px by 24px target from an invisible ::after, and cells closer than 4px overlap their targets. Evidence: measured 20px by 22px cell, src/ui/ui.css:1146. Check: review src/styles.css.
  • Don't: .layer-toggles { gap: 0 } on a touch screen.
  • Do: @media (pointer: coarse) { .layer-toggles { gap: var(--gap-4) } }
  • rule/toggle-line-height: When sm text toggles stand in a bar whose line is not 22px, set --ui-toggle-line on their container to the bar's line, because the word's target is the whole line and a 22px toggle in a 21px line makes the bar 1px taller. Evidence: measured 21px toggles in the 22px status bar under its 1px rule, in the browser, 2026-11-11. Check: review src/chrome.css.
  • Don't: .status-toggles .ui-toggle { height: 21px }
  • Do: .status-toggles { --ui-toggle-line: var(--status-line) }

Accessibility

Rests on the native <button> element with aria-pressed, the drawn glyph hidden from assistive tech. Disabled is the layer's own, shared with Button and IconButton: aria-disabled="true" with the click refused on the button itself (docs/system/decisions.md, "Disabled controls"). The state is never colour alone: the glyph changes, or the rule appears.

Related

  • IconButton: when the glyph runs an action, or one switch on a tool bar should read lit (selected).
  • Checkbox: when the yes-or-no is a form's value, or can be mixed.
  • Tab: when the control picks one view of several.
  • Tooltip: the hint box this component shows by itself; wrap another control in it, never this one.
  • Kbd: the key cap the hint draws for a shortcut.
  • Row: the list row a column of small glyph toggles sits beside; a row never nests them.

Tooltip

Description

It is the layer's one hint: a small box beside a control under the pointer or under keyboard focus, saying what the control does not already show. One box serves the whole window. Any element asks for it by carrying data-hint: the layer's components set it from their title, the Tooltip wrapper sets it on a host around another control, and a surface's own element may carry the attribute itself. It is a hint, not the control: the control keeps its own element, its own pointer, its own accessible name and its own description.

import { Tooltip } from "../../../../src/ui/Tooltip";, source src/ui/Tooltip.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/button-div, trap/hover-unguarded, trap/touch-hover-flash.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — the hover box is measured from the running Cursor 3.27.22 (docs/system/decisions.md, measured 2026-10-28): the chrome fill #141414, radius 3, the .15 hairline, the 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.4) shadow, 12px type, and the arrival over 0.1s. The placement, the delay, the dismissal, the key cap and the description are the layer's own (docs/system/decisions.md, "The hint").

Examples

<Tooltip text="Outline, the current layer"><span class="layer-name">Outline</span></Tooltip> — a hint over a control that is not a layer component.

Real uses, 1 call site (rg -c "<Tooltip" src/components → src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:1). The box itself is in use on every IconButton, Button, Chip, Tab, Field, Select, TextArea and Row that has something to say, without the wrapper. No component of the layer renders a native title attribute: Row, the last to do so, moved onto the box on 2026-11-11 (src/ui/recipe.test.ts holds every component's source to it).

  • src/components/LayersPanel.tsx — a layer row's hint.
  • src/components/StatusBar.tsx — the drafting toggles, outside the layer, carry data-hint and data-hint-keys (see "Adopting the hint outside the layer"); no native title is left in the shell.

Example: The hint over a control of a surface's own. (docs/system/examples/tooltip/default.tsx)

import { Tooltip } from "../../../../src/ui/Tooltip";

/** A fact of the status bar: the hint says what the number counts. Layer components need no wrapper. */
export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Tooltip text="Objects in the drawing" placement="top">
      <span class="status-item status-count">46 objects</span>
    </Tooltip>
  );
}

Example: The full text of a clipped chat title. (docs/system/examples/tooltip/in-assistant-head.tsx)

import { Tooltip } from "../../../../src/ui/Tooltip";

/** The pane's header: a title that clips keeps its full text in the hint, on hover and on focus. */
export default function InAssistantHead() {
  const title = "Summarise the layers and count the objects on each";
  return (
    <Tooltip text={title} placement="bottom">
      <span class="assistant-title">{title}</span>
    </Tooltip>
  );
}

Example: A status-bar fact whose hint opens above it, with a key as a cap. (docs/system/examples/tooltip/in-status-bar.tsx)

import { Tooltip } from "../../../../src/ui/Tooltip";

/**
 * At the window's foot the box has no room below and opens above by itself; `placement="top"`
 * only says so up front. The shortcut is passed by itself and drawn as a key cap, never written
 * into the text in brackets.
 */
export default function InStatusBar() {
  return (
    <Tooltip text="Snap Mode" shortcut="F9" placement="top">
      <span class="status-item">Snap on</span>
    </Tooltip>
  );
}

Variants

One shape. The box prefers the side below the control and takes the side above with placement="top"; either way it flips to the other side when the preferred one has no room (a status-bar control's hint opens above it), and slides along the window's edge rather than cross it.

What the box holds comes from three attributes on the element that asks:

AttributeHoldsDrawn as
data-hintThe hint's text.The first line.
data-hint-keysThe control's shortcut as the user reads it (Ctrl+Z, F9).One Kbd key cap after the text.
data-hint-noteA second thought: why the control is disabled, what it will do.A second line in the quieter ink.
data-hint-labelOn one element inside the control: the label the control shows, where the control's own text holds more than that label (Select holds every choice and shows one). No value.Nothing by itself: it is the text a clipped control's hint reads in full, and the text a repeated hint is compared with.
data-hint-placementtop to prefer the side above.—

A control whose label is clipped by its own box (scrollWidth past clientWidth, on the element or the label directly inside it) gets its full label as the first line by itself, and what data-hint adds drops to the second line. The label is the marked one (data-hint-label), else the part that is cut (a row's label, without the shortcut beside it), else everything the control shows; a field's label is its value, never a password's; and a part hidden from assistive tech (aria-hidden="true") is skipped, so a name drawn in pieces beside its whole text reads once.

A host that carries data-hint empty (a layer component with no title, there for its clipped label) gives way to a host around it that has words: a Tooltip wrapped around a Row still speaks. A hint that only repeats the label the control shows (compared trimmed, white space collapsed), with no shortcut and no note, is not drawn.

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
RestThe pointer is away and keyboard focus is elsewhere, or the control's hint has nothing to add.Use the control.The box is opacity: 0; visibility: hidden and takes no pointer.test
ShownA mouse or a pen rests on the host for 0.4s (at once, and without the fade, when another hint was up within the last 0.3s), or a key moves focus onto the host (Tab, an arrow key, Home, End, Page Up, Page Down, F6). Never a finger, and never focus that arrived by a click or was handed back by a closing dialog.Read the hint; the control keeps the pointer.The box fades in over 0.1s beside the host, inside the window's edges.test
DismissedEscape, a press, a click, typing, a scroll, a resize, the window losing focus, or any key in a <select> but Tab and a bare modifier (its list opens where the box sits), while the box is shown or waiting to show.Use the control; move the pointer or the focus to another control to see a hint again.The box is gone at once and stays away while the pointer rests on the same host.test
Held backThe host has its own menu or dialog open (aria-haspopup with aria-expanded="true"), or focus is inside a menu or a dialog the host is not part of.Use the menu or the dialog.No box. A control inside the open menu or dialog still hints.test

State precedence

  • Shown and Dismissed: Dismissed wins. A dismissed hint does not come back until the pointer or the focus moves to another control.
  • Shown and Held back: Held back wins. No hint draws over, or behind, the popup the person is using.
  • Dismissed and Held back: Not applicable: both draw nothing.
  • Rest and Shown: Not applicable: the box is one or the other.
  • Rest and Dismissed: Not applicable: both draw nothing.
  • Rest and Held back: Not applicable: both draw nothing.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
childrenElementThe control the hint describes.
textstringThe hint.
placement?TooltipPlacementThe side the box prefers: bottom (the default, where the platform's own hint falls, clear of the bar above a tool row) or top.
shortcut?stringThe control's shortcut as the user reads it ("Ctrl+Z", "F9"): a key cap after the text.
  • text: the hint. A short fragment: "New chat", "Copy the code".
  • shortcut: the control's shortcut as the user reads it (Ctrl+Z, F9); the box draws it as a key cap after the text. Sets data-hint-keys on the host.
  • placement: the side the box prefers, bottom (the default) or top. It flips to the other side when the preferred one has no room.
  • children: the control the hint describes. Give it its own aria-label or visible text — the hint is not the name. Not a layer component: those carry the hint themselves.

Beside the component, src/ui/Tooltip.tsx exports what a surface needs to adopt the hint without the wrapper: installHints() (wires the document once; every layer component calls it), describeByHint(el, text) (ties a hint to a control as its accessible description, from the control's ref), splitHint(title) and ariaKeyShortcuts(keys).

Adopting the hint outside the layer

A surface's own element (a status toggle, a layer key, a clipped value) moves off the native title in three steps, and needs no wrapper and no import unless it has a description to tie:

  1. Rename title to data-hint, and take a shortcut out of the text into data-hint-keys: title="Snap Mode (F9)" becomes data-hint="Snap Mode" data-hint-keys="F9". Leave no title behind. The attributes alone do not split a bracket: only IconButton and Button do that, for their existing call sites.
  2. Settle the accessible name, which the native title may have been supplying. An element with no visible text (an icon key, a colour swatch) takes the same words as aria-label. An element whose visible text is terse (SNAP) takes the full words as aria-label. An element whose visible text is already its name takes nothing.
  3. Settle the description. When the hint says more than the name and a screen-reader user needs it too (why a control is disabled, what a toggle does), tie it: ref={(el) => describeByHint(el, () => hint())}. When the hint is the element's own clipped text, tie nothing: the full text is already in the element, and the layer shows it by itself (data-hint="" is enough to opt a clipped value in). A shortcut goes on aria-keyshortcuts={ariaKeyShortcuts("F9")}.

A fact that is not a control (a <span>) takes no keyboard focus, so its hint is pointer-only: put nothing there that a keyboard user needs.

Usage

When to use

  • A control that is not a layer component needs a short hint: a toggle with a terse face, a key with a shortcut to teach.
  • A truncated value needs its full text on hover and on focus.
  • A disabled control needs to say why.

When not to use

  • The control is an icon-only action. Use IconButton instead: its title already shows in this box.
  • The control is already a layer component with a label. Use Button with its own title instead (and the same on Chip, Tab and Field): it already shows in this box.
  • The text is the control's only name. Use Button with a visible label instead.
  • The content is rich, interactive or long. Use Row rows inside a menu instead.

Rules

  • rule/tooltip-not-a-name: When a control carries a tooltip, give the control its own aria-label or visible text, because the box is aria-hidden and a control named only by its hint has 0 names for a screen reader. Evidence: single use src/ui/Tooltip.tsx:243, aria-hidden="true" on the box. Check: test src/ui/Tooltip.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tooltip text="Close"><button>✕</button></Tooltip>
  • Do: <Tooltip text="Close the panel"><button aria-label="Close the panel">✕</button></Tooltip>
  • rule/tooltip-never-blocks: When the tooltip shows, the box keeps pointer-events: none, because it sits beside the control and a hint that takes the click is worse than 0 hints. Evidence: single use src/ui/ui.css:1081, pointer-events: none on the box. Check: test src/ui/recipe.test.ts.
  • Don't: a tooltip box with a hover handler of its own.
  • Do: pointer-events: none on .ui-tooltip.
  • rule/tooltip-no-touch: When the pointer is a finger, show 0 hints, because a finger has no hover and a tap would leave the box up over the control it just pressed. Evidence: single use src/ui/Tooltip.tsx:327, the pointerType === "touch" guard. Check: test src/ui/Tooltip.test.tsx.
  • Don't: a hint that carries an instruction a touch user needs ("Hold to record").
  • Do: the instruction in the control's label or beside it, and the hint only as a repeat.
  • rule/tooltip-adds: When a hint is written for a control with a visible label, write what the label leaves out and 0 words that repeat it, because the layer draws no box for a hint equal to the label and a description equal to the name is read twice. Evidence: single use src/ui/Tooltip.tsx:203, the comparison of the hint with the label the control shows. Check: test src/ui/Tooltip.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tooltip text="Check connection"><button type="button">Check connection</button></Tooltip>
  • Do: <Tooltip text="Check the address and the key"><button type="button">Check connection</button></Tooltip>
  • rule/tooltip-shortcut-cap: When a hint teaches a shortcut, pass it by itself (shortcut, data-hint-keys) and keep it out of the text, because the box draws 1 key cap for it and text in brackets is read as part of the sentence. Evidence: app 9/31 icon buttons in the running shell end their title in a bracketed shortcut, which IconButton and Button still split off for them, measured in the browser 2026-11-11. Check: test src/ui/Tooltip.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <button data-hint="Snap Mode (F9)" aria-label="Snap Mode">SNAP</button>
  • Do: <button data-hint="Snap Mode" data-hint-keys="F9" aria-label="Snap Mode" aria-keyshortcuts="F9">SNAP</button>

Content

  • rule/tooltip-text-fragment: When the hint's text is written, keep it a fragment of 1 to 4 words in sentence case with no full stop ("Copy the code", not "Click here to copy."), because the box is one 24px line for a fragment and a sentence is read as a paragraph; a reason a control is disabled is the exception and is 1 sentence. Evidence: app 31/31 icon button hints in the running shell are 4 words or fewer before the bracket, measured in the browser 2026-11-11. Check: review src/components/ToolStrip.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tooltip text="This button will close the assistant panel.">
  • Do: <Tooltip text="Close the panel">

Anti-slop

  • rule/tooltip-one-hint: When a control shows this hint, keep it the control's 1 hint: move the text out of the native title into text or data-hint, and leave a layer component unwrapped, because two hints stack: the platform's box arrives on its own delay over the layer's, and a layer component already shows its own. Evidence: app 31/31 icon buttons in the running shell render no title attribute, measured in the browser 2026-11-11. Check: test src/ui/Tooltip.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Tooltip text="Snap Mode"><button title="Snap Mode (F9)">Snap</button></Tooltip>
  • Do: <Tooltip text="Snap Mode" shortcut="F9"><button aria-label="Snap Mode">Snap</button></Tooltip>

Limits

  • rule/tooltip-length-limit: When a hint runs past 64 characters, move the explanation into the control's label or help text, because the box wraps at a 32ch measure (207px at 12px type) and a third line reads as a paragraph over the surface it covers. Evidence: measured 207px by 40px box, 2 lines, for the 46-character "To save, choose a provider or type a base URL." at 1280px and at 390px, src/ui/ui.css:1066. Check: test src/ui/recipe.test.ts.
  • Don't: a 120-character hint over the composer.
  • Do: a 3-word hint and a visible line of help for the rest.

Accessibility

The box is for the eye and is hidden from assistive tech; the same words reach a screen reader through the control. Where the hint is the control's name (an icon key), the name is on aria-label. Where the control has a visible label and the hint adds to it, the hint is the control's description: describeByHint keeps the words in a hidden line on <body> and points aria-describedby at it. aria-describedby rather than aria-description, because the second is an ARIA 1.3 draft attribute and the desktop app runs in whatever system webview the machine has (docs/system/decisions.md, "The hint"). The host of the wrapper is a plain <span>, so the child's semantics are unchanged. It meets WCAG 1.4.13 as dismissable (Escape) and persistent (it stays while the pointer or the focus does); it is not hoverable, which the criterion allows for a box that only repeats what the control's own name and description say and takes no pointer.

Keyboard

KeyWhere focus isEffectFocus afterChecked by
TabThe control.The box shows at once, and goes when focus leaves the host.Stays on the control.test
EscapeAnywhere, the box showing.Puts the box away; the key is not consumed, so a surface that closes on Escape still closes. Focus the closing surface hands back raises no hint.Unchanged.test
EnterThe control, the box showing.The control's click puts the box away.Unchanged.test
A character keyA field, the box showing.Typing puts the box away.Stays in the field.test

ARIA

PartRoleAccessible name fromStates and propertiesAnnouncedChecked by
The boxNone: aria-hidden="true"——Nothingtest
The hostNone: a plain <span> carrying data-hint——Nothingtest
The controlUnchanged (its own role)Its own aria-label or textaria-describedby when describeByHint ties the hint; aria-keyshortcuts for a shortcutIts name, then the descriptiontest
The descriptionNone: a <span> in the hidden .ui-hint-descriptions element on <body>—Referenced by aria-describedby; removed with its controlRead after the control's name and roletest

Related

  • IconButton: shows this box by itself from its title, shortcut and description; never wrap one.
  • Button: shows this box from its title, which is its description; never wrap one.
  • Tab: shows its clipped label in this box by itself.
  • Chip: the pickable keyword form; its title shows here.
  • Field: its title shows here and joins its description.
  • Kbd: the key cap the box draws for a shortcut; and the pick when the key should stay on the surface rather than show on hover.

rule/tab-md-label-limitWhen an md tab's label runs past 24 characters, pass the whole label as the children and leave the shortening to the tab, because the tab clips at max-width: 24ch with an ellipsis and shows the full label in its hint by itself, and uncapped the 56-character "A1 Ground floor general arrangement plan, sheet 12 of 40" draws a 357.8px tab that pushes the other layouts out of the strip.components/tabmeasuredtest src/ui/Tab.test.tsx
rule/tab-selected-markedWhen a strip has a tab in front, pass selected on it, because the fill alone is colour and a screen reader needs aria-selected="true" to hear which view shows.components/tabapptest src/ui/Tab.test.tsx
rule/tab-touch-targetWhen sm tabs are laid out in a pane header, leave the header room for a 24px tab, because under a coarse pointer the 22px tab grows to the 24px control height (it clips its own overflow for the ellipsis, so it cannot take an overhanging target) and a header fixed at 22px would cut it.components/tabmeasuredreview src/ui/ui.css
rule/textarea-bare-card-focusWhen variant="bare" is used, give the card around it the focus cue with :focus-within, because the bare editor draws 0 rings of its own and a keyboard user would otherwise see no focus at all.components/textareasingle usereview src/assistant.css
rule/textarea-canonical-elementWhen a surface needs multi-line text, render TextArea rather than a raw <textarea> with its own class and its own grow function, because the hand-built one fixes its limits in pixels (64 and 240) where the type size they were counted from can change, and every copy re-solves composition and growth.components/textareasingle usereview src/ui/TextArea.tsx
rule/textarea-combobox-while-listedWhen a text area drives a list of matches for part of what is typed, pass role="combobox" with expanded, controls and activeDescendant only while the list shows, and drop all 4 when it goes, because a multi-line text box that always says it is a combobox is announced as 1 on every focus, and its arrow keys are then expected to walk a list that is not there.components/textareaapptest src/ui/TextArea.test.tsx
rule/textarea-described-byWhen a line of help, a count or an error sits beside a text area, give the line an id and pass it as describedBy, and pass invalid while the text is refused, because a line that only sits near the control is read 0 times by a screen reader that lands on it by Tab.components/textareasingle usetest src/ui/TextArea.test.tsx
rule/textarea-enter-in-keydownWhen Enter sends the text, handle it in onKeyDown and call preventDefault, leaving Shift+Enter to break the line, because onKeyDown hears 0 keys while an input method is composing and a handler on a wrapper would send a half-composed word.components/textareasingle usetest src/ui/TextArea.test.tsx
rule/textarea-label-boundWhen a text area is rendered without a visible <label>, pass ariaLabel, because a placeholder disappears at the first character and leaves 1 unnamed text box.components/textareasingle usetest src/ui/TextArea.test.tsx
rule/textarea-max-rowsWhen text may run past 8 lines, leave maxRows at 8 or set it to the lines the surface can spare (9 in the composer), because past the cap the box stops and scrolls, and a cap the surface cannot hold pushes the send key off the screen.components/textareameasuredtest src/ui/TextArea.test.tsx
rule/textarea-one-row-fieldWhen a text area sits on a row with a Field, pass rows={1}, because 1 line of the field variant measures the Field's 24px and the default 2 lines measure 40px.components/textareameasuredreview src/ui/ui.css
rule/textarea-placeholder-exampleWhen a placeholder is written, show in 2 to 6 words what goes here or what the control takes (Ask, or / for commands) and put a rule the user must keep in mind in a line tied by describedBy, because the placeholder is gone at the first character.components/textareasingle usereview src/components/AssistantPane.tsx
rule/textarea-rows-not-heightWhen a text area needs a smallest or a largest size, pass rows and maxRows rather than a height, min-height or max-height in a stylesheet, because the component sets the height itself from the measured text on every edit and a second height fights it by 1 line or more.components/textareasingle usetest src/ui/TextArea.test.tsx
rule/toggle-canonical-elementWhen a surface needs an on-off key, render Toggle rather than a raw <button aria-pressed> with its own class, because the 2 replaced families (.toggle, .status-toggle) each carried their own hover, ring and state inks and neither had a disabled state or a touch target.components/toggleapplint node scripts/check-system.mjs --root .
rule/toggle-disabled-reasonWhen a toggle is disabled by something the person can change, pass the reason as description in 1 short sentence, because the disabled toggle stays focusable for exactly this, and hint is not exposed to a screen reader.components/togglesingle usetest src/ui/Toggle.test.tsx
rule/toggle-group-one-stopWhen more than 3 toggles stand in one bar, give the bar role="toolbar" with a name and make it 1 Tab stop (the container sets each tabIndex; the arrows, Home and End move), because 11 Tab stops in the status bar stand between the drawing and everything after it.components/togglesingle usereview src/components/StatusBar.tsx
rule/toggle-label-settingWhen ariaLabel is written, name the setting as a noun phrase of 1 to 4 words that is true while the toggle is pressed (Outline frozen, Snap mode), in sentence case, because it is read with "pressed" or "not pressed" after it, and a verb there reads as a command.components/toggleappreview src/components/StatusBar.tsx
rule/toggle-line-heightWhen sm text toggles stand in a bar whose line is not 22px, set --ui-toggle-line on their container to the bar's line, because the word's target is the whole line and a 22px toggle in a 21px line makes the bar 1px taller.components/togglemeasuredreview src/chrome.css
rule/toggle-name-fixedWhen a toggle is rendered, pass 1 ariaLabel that names the setting and is the same string in both states, and put the action in hint, because aria-pressed already says the state, and a name that flips between Freeze and Thaw is heard as 2 different buttons.components/toggleapptest src/ui/Toggle.test.tsx
rule/toggle-no-fillWhen a toggle should look on, pass pressed and add 0 background rules of the surface's own, because the glyph, the ink or the rule already says so, and 1 fill per pressed key turns a list where nearly every row is on into a column of fills.components/togglemeasuredtest src/ui/recipe.test.ts
rule/toggle-no-native-titleWhen a toggle is styled or wrapped, add 0 hints of its own (no title attribute set from outside, no Tooltip around it), because the component already shows hint in the layer's hint box and a second hint stacks on the first.components/toggleapptest src/ui/Toggle.test.tsx
rule/toggle-owns-nothingWhen onChange runs, set the caller's own value from its argument (or refuse it), because the toggle draws from pressed after every press and keeps 0 state of its own.components/togglesingle usetest src/ui/Toggle.test.tsx
rule/toggle-state-in-faceWhen a glyph toggle is rendered, pass 2 icons (icon for off, iconOn for on), because the toggle draws no fill at rest and the ink alone would carry the state by colour only.components/toggleappreview src/components/LayersPanel.tsx
rule/toggle-text-shortWhen a text face is written, pass 1 word of at most 6 letters and the full name as ariaLabel and hint, because the bar holds 11 of them on one line at 1280 wide and the capitals are tracked.components/toggleappreview src/components/StatusBar.tsx
rule/toggle-tone-meaningWhen a tone is passed, pick it by which state the person must notice (absent for off, info or caution for on) and pass 1 tone per setting across the whole list, because the tone is the only colour in the column and a tone picked for looks makes 2 rows of the same setting read as different things.components/toggleappreview src/components/LayersPanel.tsx
rule/toggle-touch-targetWhen 2 sm glyph toggles sit side by side, keep at least 4px between them under a coarse pointer, because each 20px by 22px cell keeps its drawn size there and takes a 24px by 24px target from an invisible ::after, and cells closer than 4px overlap their targets.components/togglemeasuredreview src/styles.css
rule/token-parityA var(--x) or @theme reference no CSS file defines, or a color key that :root and a dark theme block do not both definenone yetscripts/check-system.mjs
rule/tooltip-addsWhen a hint is written for a control with a visible label, write what the label leaves out and 0 words that repeat it, because the layer draws no box for a hint equal to the label and a description equal to the name is read twice.components/tooltipsingle usetest src/ui/Tooltip.test.tsx
rule/tooltip-length-limitWhen a hint runs past 64 characters, move the explanation into the control's label or help text, because the box wraps at a 32ch measure (207px at 12px type) and a third line reads as a paragraph over the surface it covers.components/tooltipmeasuredtest src/ui/recipe.test.ts
rule/tooltip-never-blocksWhen the tooltip shows, the box keeps pointer-events: none, because it sits beside the control and a hint that takes the click is worse than 0 hints.components/tooltipsingle usetest src/ui/recipe.test.ts
rule/tooltip-no-touchWhen the pointer is a finger, show 0 hints, because a finger has no hover and a tap would leave the box up over the control it just pressed.components/tooltipsingle usetest src/ui/Tooltip.test.tsx
rule/tooltip-not-a-nameWhen a control carries a tooltip, give the control its own aria-label or visible text, because the box is aria-hidden and a control named only by its hint has 0 names for a screen reader.components/tooltipsingle usetest src/ui/Tooltip.test.tsx
rule/tooltip-one-hintWhen a control shows this hint, keep it the control's 1 hint: move the text out of the native title into text or data-hint, and leave a layer component unwrapped, because two hints stack: the platform's box arrives on its own delay over the layer's, and a layer component already shows its own.components/tooltip, decisionsapptest src/ui/Tooltip.test.tsx
rule/tooltip-shortcut-capWhen a hint teaches a shortcut, pass it by itself (shortcut, data-hint-keys) and keep it out of the text, because the box draws 1 key cap for it and text in brackets is read as part of the sentence.components/tooltipapptest src/ui/Tooltip.test.tsx
rule/tooltip-text-fragmentWhen the hint's text is written, keep it a fragment of 1 to 4 words in sentence case with no full stop ("Copy the code", not "Click here to copy."), because the box is one 24px line for a fragment and a sentence is read as a paragraph; a reason a control is disabled is the exception and is 1 sentence.components/tooltipappreview src/components/ToolStrip.tsx

What the check can't see

A reviewer or a browser covers these. Passing cd apps/ui && bun run check says nothing about them.

  • Rendered contrast, including non-text contrast of borders, focus rings and checkbox edges. Measure it in a browser.
  • Behavior: what a click, Enter or Escape does, focus order and focus return, and whether Cancel submits.
  • Layout at each viewport, overflow at 390px and touch target sizes.
  • Visual overrides on components the registry does not list, and overrides built at runtime: cn() branches, spread props, a class name held in a variable.
  • A loading state shown some other way than a label ternary on the button, such as a label read from a variable.
  • Class names and values built at runtime, such as template strings, cn() branches or fontSize: size / 2.5.
  • bg-white and text-black when the theme defines no role for their job, their opacity forms such as bg-black/50, and CSS keywords such as white in var() fallbacks.
  • Files outside the include folders, and ui files missing from the drift list (they are scanned, but no hash guards them).
  • Whether a token's role comment still matches how the token is used.
  • Rules the generated rules page marks review, or enforces only through their own Check: clause.
  • Motion that is only measured: exit slower than enter, frequent-surface motion, linear easing, press delay, input lag and jank. Easing set in script or through a variable, and hover reveals written as Tailwind classes (v4 guards hover: itself, v3 does not).
  • Whether a pressed style covers the control whose tap highlight was removed: any pressed style in the repo passes trap/touch-tap-highlight.

The web system's design decisions

The lock for the SolidJS UI (apps/ui), taken in the design-system run of 2026-10-28. The design source is the running Cursor 3.27.22 desktop app, measured live (.design-system/research/cursor-recipes-2026-10-28.md). The values live in src/tokens.css; this file records the picks and the reasons, so the next surface does not re-litigate them.

Canonical picks

The web UI grows thirteen canonical components under src/ui/, each a thin wrapper over the native element. The per-surface hand-rolled classes they replace are named below; a class loses because it is a one-off with no shared API and no states.

  • Button — pick ui/Button.tsx (native <button>). Variants primary | secondary | ghost | danger, default secondary (Cursor's own default button). Loses: .button (TopBar — one call site), .assistant-send / .assistant-save / .assistant-ghost (assistant-only, their own colours), .assistant-preset (a suggestion chip wearing a button), .tool-button (ToolStrip — a grid cell, no variants), .menu-row (a menu item, not a general button).
  • IconButton — pick ui/IconButton.tsx (native <button>, a drawn icon + label). Variants ghost | soft | inverted; sizes md (24px) and sm (20px). Loses: .assistant-icon (three uses, fixed 24px, no variant), .assistant-attachment-x (one-off). The layer list's state keys and the status bar's drafting toggles were listed here as its losers until 2026-11-11 and never moved: they are Toggle's (below).
  • Chip — pick ui/Chip.tsx (native <button> when interactive, <span> when not). Loses: .chip (TopBar — a static fact, no interaction), .keyword-chip (CommandLine — interactive, no tone/size API), .cmd-chips (a container, not a chip).
  • Field — pick ui/Field.tsx (native <input>, single-line). Variants field | inline, sizes md (24px) and sm (20px), align start | end, as Select ("A value in a dense row" below). Loses: .assistant-input, .cmd-input, .prop-input (each one surface's own padding and border), .assistant-field (a label wrapper, not the control). The composer's auto-growing <textarea> and the properties palette's <select> were found-not-fixed here until 2026-11-11; TextArea and Select below are their picks.
  • Select — pick ui/Select.tsx (a native <select> under a drawn face: keyboard, type-ahead, a phone's picker and every system webview's own list are the platform's; no hand-built listbox). Variants field | inline, sizes md (24px) and sm (20px), align start | end. The value is drawn in a <span> over the control, which is what lets it end in an ellipsis before the arrow, end on the arrow's side and read quieter while mixed the same way in all three webviews. Loses: .prop-select (PropertiesPanel — appearance: none with no arrow drawn in its place, a long value cut with no ellipsis, the off-list option and the *VARIES* ink done by hand).
  • Checkbox — pick ui/Checkbox.tsx (a native <input type="checkbox"> inside its <label>, the box and the mark drawn from tokens). No variants; states checked, mixed, disabled. Loses: .prop-check (PropertiesPanel — the platform's own box tinted with accent-color, a different shape and tick in each webview, 13px with no touch target).
  • TextArea — pick ui/TextArea.tsx (a native <textarea> that measures its own height between rows and maxRows). Variants field | bare. Loses: .assistant-input with its grow function (AssistantPane — the limits fixed at 64px and 240px beside a type size that can change).
  • Row — pick ui/Row.tsx (native <button>, the full-width clickable band). Loses: .prop-row, .menu-row, .assistant-row, .assistant-tool (each repeats hover/selected padding by hand). A grid row carrying nested controls of its own (.layer-row with its toggle cluster) stays bespoke — a button cannot nest buttons. The pilot kept .assistant-row (the composer's toolbar is a container with nested buttons) and .assistant-tool (a transcript disclosure row, not a menu band) bespoke for the same reason; row.md records it. Inside a role="listbox" that keeps the keyboard in its own field, the row is <Row option>: the role="option" element itself, with no Tab stop and no hover fill of its own ("A row in a listbox" below). Loses there: .palette-option (CommandPalette — a wrapper div carrying the option role around a Row button).
  • SectionLabel — pick ui/SectionLabel.tsx (native <h2> — a heading, so a screen reader can jump between panels). Loses: .section-label (already shared but untyped — the pick is its typed home), .properties-head / .layers-head (the surrounding bar, not the label), .assistant-title (a pane title, a different role).
  • Tooltip — pick ui/Tooltip.tsx: the layer's one hint, a single box on <body> placed beside whichever control carries data-hint. Every layer component that takes title carries it; the <Tooltip> wrapper (a <span> host; the child keeps its own element and its own accessible name) and the bare data-hint attribute give it to a surface's own element. Placements bottom | top, flipped and held inside the window by itself; it never takes the pointer. Loses: the native title attribute as an icon key's hint (it arrives on the platform's own delay, in the platform's own box, and never on keyboard focus), and any per-surface hover label a panel would draw for itself. The reasons are under "The hint" below.
  • Tab — pick ui/Tab.tsx (native <button> with role="tab", aria-selected on the one in front; an optional close key as a sibling button). Sizes md (the editor tab, selected at --tab-active) and sm (the compact tab of a pane header, selected at --fill-active). Loses: .layout-tab (StatusBar's layout strip — a raw button with its own class), the chat tabs' Row workaround (AssistantPane — a Row in a width cell beside a close IconButton).
  • Toggle — pick ui/Toggle.tsx (native <button aria-pressed>, the state drawn by the face alone). Variants glyph | text; sizes sm (the cell of a 22px row, the status bar's line) and md (24px); tones neutral | absent | info | caution. Loses: .toggle with .is-on / .is-frozen / .is-locked (LayersPanel — three raw buttons per row, the tone picked by :first-child and a class), .status-toggle (StatusBar — a raw button with its own hover, ring and on rule). The reasons are under "A setting switched in place" below.
  • Kbd — pick ui/Kbd.tsx (native <kbd>, one recipe, no variants). Loses: .assistant-key (AssistantPane — the mono face at the disabled ink), .palette-key (CommandPalette — the recipe kept, now the pick's own).

Prop vocabulary

  • variant: primary | secondary | ghost | danger (default secondary) — purpose, not appearance.
  • size: sm | md (default md).
  • plus disabled, selected, title.
  • IconButton expanded and controls: a fold key says whether the region it folds is showing (aria-expanded) and which region it is (aria-controls, the region's id). A key is a fold key or a selected toggle, never both.
  • IconButton popup: menu | dialog | listbox (aria-haspopup), beside expanded and controls, on a key that opens something floating over the page. menu when what opens is a list of actions (role="menu": the narrow window's Main menu), listbox when it is a list of values to pick one from (role="listbox": a model picker), dialog when it holds fields or other controls (role="dialog": the provider form). A fold key that shows a region in the page's own flow takes no popup.
  • title is the layer's hint on every component that takes it, and no component renders a native title attribute. What it is to assistive tech depends on whether the control has a visible label: on IconButton (a glyph, no label) it is the name (aria-label); on Button, Chip, Tab, Row, Field, Select and TextArea (a label, or ariaLabel) it is the description (aria-describedby), never the name. "The hint" below has the reasons.
  • Button and IconButton shortcut: the shortcut as the user reads it (Ctrl+Z), drawn as a key cap in the hint and said through aria-keyshortcuts. data-hint-keys is the same thing on an element outside the layer.
  • IconButton description: the second line of the hint and the key's accessible description (aria-describedby): why it is disabled, what it will do. Button needs no such prop: its title already is its description.
  • disabled on Button and IconButton is aria-disabled="true", never the native attribute ("Disabled controls" below). Field, Select, Checkbox, TextArea and Row keep the native disabled; a Row option is not a native control and says aria-disabled="true".
  • Field autocomplete and spellcheck: the native attributes, passed through; unset leaves each to the platform, except that a password field is never spell-checked. A secret passes autocomplete="off" and spellcheck={false} whatever type it shows at the moment.
  • Field invalid and describedBy: a refused value says so (aria-invalid="true", the error stroke), and the help line or the error line under a field is tied to it by id (aria-describedby). describedBy is the layer's name for that tie on any component that grows one, as ariaLabel is for the name.
  • Button ariaLabel (the name Field already uses for the same job): the accessible name, only where the visible label is a value rather than the action; it starts with the action and holds the visible text.
  • ariaLabel, describedBy, invalid and title mean on Select and TextArea what they mean on Field; Checkbox takes ariaLabel (when it has no visible label) and describedBy.
  • variant on the value controls names where the control sits, not how it looks: Select and Field field | inline (a form control; a value in a dense list row that reads as text until touched), TextArea field | bare (a form control; the editor inside a card that draws the box and shows the focus itself).
  • Select and Field align: start | end, the side of the box the value sits on (end in a column of values; on Field it also sets lining tabular figures, so a column of numbers lines up).
  • mixed (Select, Checkbox, Field): the control stands for several things whose values differ. Select shows its placeholder, which is never a choice; Checkbox sets indeterminate and aria-checked="mixed"; Field draws the stand-in the caller passes as its value in the quiet ink.
  • Field readOnly, maxLength, inputMode: the native attributes, passed through. readOnly is not disabled: the value can be focused, selected and copied.
  • Field selectOnFocus: the whole value is selected as focus arrives, by key or by click, so typing replaces it; a second click places the caret.
  • Field onKeyDown, onFocus, onBlur, ref: the pass-throughs a value that commits on Enter and on leaving needs. onKeyDown never hears a key an input method is using, as on TextArea.
  • role, expanded, controls, activeDescendant, autocompleteKind (Field, TextArea): a text control that drives a list of matches and keeps the keyboard is a combobox. role takes only combobox; expanded and controls mean what they mean on IconButton (aria-expanded, aria-controls); activeDescendant is the id of the option the arrow keys are on (aria-activedescendant); autocompleteKind is aria-autocomplete (list | inline | both | none), named apart from autocomplete, which is the platform's autofill. They are passed together or not at all: on Field for as long as the field exists (the palette's input), on TextArea only while its list shows (the composer's slash list), and Row option rows are the list.
  • onChange(value) on a control whose value is picked (Select, Checkbox) and onInput(value) on one whose value is typed (Field, TextArea): each hands back the value, not the event. The caller owns the value on all four, and Select and Checkbox redraw from their props after every pick, so a change the caller refuses does not stay drawn.
  • Select options: the choices as data ({ value, label, disabled? }[]), never children; a value that is not among them is listed first by the component.
  • TextArea rows and maxRows: the fewest lines shown and the most before it scrolls; the height between is measured, and no stylesheet sets one.
  • TextArea onKeyDown, onPaste, ref: the pass-throughs a composer needs. onKeyDown never hears a key an input method is using.
  • Row option, with id and onPointerMove: the row is one option of a listbox that owns the focus and the highlight.
  • Row title: the hint and the row's description in both forms, as on Button; the name stays the row's text.
  • Chip tone: neutral | accent.
  • Toggle pressed and onChange(pressed): the state and the state a press asks for, as checked and onChange on Checkbox; the caller owns it. selected stays IconButton's word for a key that is lit while on.
  • Toggle ariaLabel and hint: the fixed name and the hint are two props because they are two strings ("Outline frozen", "Thaw"). title is not taken: on every other component it is the hint and also the name or the description, and a toggle's hint is neither. description, shortcut and disabled mean what they mean on IconButton, and placement what it means on Tooltip.
  • Toggle variant: glyph | text, the face. Toggle tone: neutral | absent | info | caution, which state is the one to notice and its ink; it names the meaning, and the token layer picks the colour per theme.
  • Toggle icon and iconOn: the glyph of each state. Toggle tabIndex: the one pass-through for a group that is one Tab stop; unset, the component writes no attribute.
  • No boolean style props (round, big, blue): a prop names a purpose; the token layer picks the look.

Motion presets

One job, one preset (durations and easings from tokens.css):

  • press → --dur-press + --ease-standard: the transform channel only (the icon button's scale to .98). A fill that changes under a press takes the hover preset.
  • hover / focus feedback → --dur-fast + --ease-standard: the measured state transition, .1s ease (research §8: 24 declarations in the glass UI, and the button families' color, background-color channels). This line read --ease-out until 2026-11-11; the measurement and src/tokens.css say ease, the layer (src/ui/ui.css) already drew it, and the page was the side that moved.
  • open (menu, popover, composer focus) → --dur-med + --ease-out-quint.
  • close → --dur-fast + --ease-out.
  • panel / larger change → --dur-slow + --ease-out. Reserved: no panel moves yet, and --dur-slow is kept in src/tokens.css for this line alone, so the first panel that moves does not pick its own duration.
  • hint → arrives on the hover / focus preset (opacity), leaves at once. The wait before it is script, not a token: 0.4s under a resting pointer, none on keyboard focus, none for 0.3s after another hint went away; and that next hint arrives without the fade too, because a fade restarting on every key of a row is a flicker.
  • Reduced motion: the app's data-animations attribute already gates motion; the presets keep it — no preset plays when animations are off. The hint also answers the platform's own setting (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce): it is a box the layer hangs on <body> for every surface, so it does not wait for the shell to mirror the setting into the attribute.

Icon sizes

  • 14px glyph in a 24px control — icon buttons.
  • 16px glyph in a 28px control — tool strip / buttons.
  • 12px glyph in a 20px control — chips.
  • Icons stay code-drawn (src/icons.ts); no new icon assets (project rule: no third-party iconography).

What follows the drawing

Tokens left untouched because they describe the document, not the chrome: --canvas, --grid-minor, --grid-major, --axis-x, --axis-y, --layer-current, --icon-layer-*, --icon-locked, --swatch-border, --control, --control-hover, --cmd-bg, --cmd-border, and the dark --warn / --error / --toggle-on (already Cursor's, §1). Geometry that was not re-measured also stays: --dur-med, --ease-out, the other radii, the gaps, control heights, fonts. src/canvas.ts reads the model-space colours (--canvas, --grid-*, --axis-*, --selection) from the CSS custom properties at runtime, so the drawing and the chrome cannot drift.

A token with no reader is a value nobody checks: it drifts (the light --icon-point had been corrected for contrast on a glyph no surface drew) and it invites a second way to do a thing the layer already does.

  • --list-bg: no rule paints it, but src/ui/recipe.test.ts and scripts/contrast-report.mjs
